sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
Industrial AI is entering a new phase. After decades of predictive analytics and other specialized applications, advances in foundation models, physical AI, and agentic AI are making it possible to automate more complex tasks across industrial environments. But unlike AI that operates purely in the digital world, industrial AI can interact directly with physical systems, where an unexpected decision can have consequences for safety, reliability, and critical infrastructure.

That makes responsible deployment central to the next wave of industrial automation. “How do we leverage these technologies while maintaining safety, while maintaining reliable operations, while still being able to deliver on the promises of the new capabilities?” asks Arti Garg, chief technologist at AVEVA. The challenge is particularly acute as newer AI systems become more capable but also harder to predict and explain.

One foundation for making that transition work is data. Industrial systems often contain information across telemetry, service logs, engineering documents, and other disparate sources. Newer technologies can help connect and correlate that information more quickly, giving operators real-time support when diagnosing problems. AI-powered robots could take that a step further by gathering information in hazardous environments without requiring workers to enter them.

But greater autonomy also requires new approaches to governance. AVEVA’s framework for responsible AI emphasizes security, efficiency, and human safety and oversight. Garg argues that AI should augment rather than replace people in critical decision loops, with guardrails determining where automated systems can act and where human supervisors remain responsible.

Sustainability is another part of that equation. AI can help manage complex power systems as renewable generation grows, while organizations also need better ways to understand AI’s own environmental footprint. Garg is involved in an IEEE working group developing a standard methodology for measuring that impact across electricity, energy, resources, water, and carbon.

The next phase could bring industrial AI further into the physical world, from autonomous robots and drones to AI-assisted coding that allows domain experts to build new applications. But realizing that potential will require more than deploying new technology, says Garg. Organizations will need to rethink business processes, establish appropriate safeguards, and give experienced workers new ways to apply their expertise, creating a model of automation that is not only more autonomous, but safer, more efficient, and more sustainable.

“Autonomous systems, whether they’re robots or drones, are really going to change the way that we work in plants, in power systems, on mining sites,” says Garg. “In a way, that will make these types of operations more efficient, much safer for the human beings involved and more productive.”

This episode of Business Lab is produced in partnership with AVEVA.

Megan Tatum: From MIT Technology Review, I’m Megan Tatum, and this is Business Lab, the show that helps business leaders make sense of new technologies coming out of the lab and into the marketplace.

Industrial AI may not be new, but it is developing at a breakneck pace. From modern predictive analytics that can preempt equipment failures, to autonomous robots tasked with inspecting high risk machinery, emerging applications have the potential to transform operational efficiencies. But often used in high consequence environments with minimal margin for error, industrial AI deployed without clarity, security, or accountability could also have catastrophic consequences for critical infrastructure over time. As industries rush to embrace the latest technologies, the goal should always be responsible AI designed to support, rather than replace that all important human judgment.

Two words for you: sustainable automation.

My guest today is Arti Garg, chief technologist at AVEVA.

This podcast is produced in partnership with AVEVA.

Arti Garg: Thank you, Megan. It’s great to be here.

Megan: Thank you so much for joining us. And just to start, if we could set some context for our discussion, can you share a bit about the current state of industrial AI and what AVEVA is working on at the moment as well?

Arti: Yeah, more than happy to. And I want to go back to what you already stated, which is that in some ways, industrial AI is not new. It’s something that, even here at AVEVA, we’ve been working on for more than 20 years, really thinking about how AI can enhance applications in the industrial sector.

But what has changed quite substantially in maybe the last few years is the type of AI. We’ve really moved to these general purpose foundation models, which enable a lot more people to leverage advanced AI technologies. In addition to that, in just the last couple of years, there’s been an explosion in what’s known as physical AI and the types of AI that can really accelerate the capabilities of robotics and autonomous systems. And also agentic AI, which also allows for automation at more of the software level.

And what we’re seeing is that while in the past there has been some hesitancy to adopt models that don’t totally have predictable outcomes, there’s been a rapid acceleration in adoption of AI even in the industrial sector. One study suggests maybe that’s almost a 78% increase over the past just two years within the industrial sector. So yes, that’s an inflection point, but it’s almost like a step function if you think about it with respect to AI adoption.

And what we’re really thinking about now at AVEVA is, how do we think about this? How do we think about incorporating these new and very powerful AI technologies in environments where customers have mission-critical operations, human safety is a significant factor? Those are some of the primary concerns that our customers have when they think about adopting any new technology. We’re doing that in narrow where these newer types of AI aren’t necessarily predictable, in terms of how they behave. That’s one of the areas we’re really thinking about is, how do we leverage these technologies while maintaining safety, while maintaining reliable operations, while still being able to deliver on the promises of the new capabilities?

Megan: There’s so many things to consider at once, isn’t it? And you outlined there some of the huge developments we’ve seen in this space in recent years. What makes this such a pivotal moment for industrial AI specifically? What has changed to make some of those perhaps more out there hypotheticals much more plausible?

Arti: Well, I think one of the big things, one of the big challenges within industrial AI, and this is something that as AVEVA, it’s in our blood, it’s in our core DNA, is that to really leverage any kind of digital technology in the industrial space, one of the first important things you often need to do is gather and correlate data from disparate systems, so that maybe I have telemetry coming off of a pump or a mixer, and I want to be able to correlate that with service logs so I know maybe the last time that someone had done some maintenance on that pump or mixer. And maybe I also want to be able to correlate that with the original design documentation and some of the original documentation on how to maintain that, so that if something is happening, I can do a better job diagnosing what’s going wrong and how to address it. This has always been a core challenge in the industrial space.

I think that what’s happening now is that with newer technologies, even things like graph databases and being able to leverage AI to really match disparate data sets much faster, we’re able to get to the point where if something goes wrong, instead of an operator maybe needing to spend a little bit of time doing this research to really understand how do these different components fit together of information, they may have just an iPad with an AI that can very quickly go and fetch that information, correlate it and help in real time, almost, diagnose what is happening.

Even a little bit more out there, but not as out there as you might think is, I still describe this with a human operator with potentially a mobile tablet, but imagine now I can also have a robot moving through that environment also gathering data and either with onboard computation or a quick connection to an operator who doesn’t necessarily now have to go out into a dangerous, potentially somewhat hazardous space, be able to gather data and enable that very quick diagnostic as well. And I think that’s really what’s exciting right now and what all of these new technologies that I’ve talked about are helping to enable.

And I think then from our perspective, trying to really leverage all of those means that we have to think a lot now about our governance approach to this. How do we leverage AI in a way that keeps it contained, if you will?

Megan: Yeah, absolutely. And on that governance point, how does AVEVA define responsible AI and what do you see as the primary benefits?

Arti: Yeah, so I think for us, we think about a triple mandate around responsible AI, and that means that it’s secure, it’s efficient, and that includes environmentally efficient, and then it really preserves human safety and human oversight above all. And for us, that’s what some of our core pillars of responsible AI include. And for us, that means we think about internally as we build tools, a multi-layered governance approach where we’ve got both for how we use AI as a company and then how we deploy AI into our products. We’ve got a similar framework that we leverage across both, a kind of joint governance model, both around how we’re leveraging AI and also how we’re infusing AI into our products to allow our customers to leverage AI in their operations.

But I would say one of the core foundational principles underneath all of these is that human beings still remain centered in how we think about how AI is leveraged. And so human judgment, human responsibility, human ethics are still core to how we think about where AI can add benefits, and we think about it more as augmenting rather than replacing human beings in critical decision loops, if you will.

Megan: Right, which is such an important distinction, isn’t it? And in terms of the next phase of development, there’s growing sentiment that agentic AI will soon allow these industrial systems to operate much more autonomously. I wonder, what makes the risks in industrial settings different from AI risk in a purely digital context? And I suppose on the flip side, what are the benefits and opportunities of that same software defined automation?

Arti: I think we can start with the risks and then go to the benefits. I think ultimately, I would say the biggest risk in the industrial setting is that we are interacting with real physical systems, often physical systems that are very capable of delivering important outcomes that keep our world running, whether that’s delivering power, whether that’s mining for natural resources. But usually. Those physical systems are also operating in hazardous environments, the equipment itself is capable of also having human safety implications. Anytime you’re interfacing software with a physical system that can have real world consequences, you have to be extra careful. And we’ve always had that, again, we’ve had that in our DNA at AVEVA from the beginning, being mindful of that end user and that end application, which is not just something on a computer screen.

Even as we’ve deployed AI over the past few decades into our systems, we’ve typically leaned toward really trying to pick the best fit model, really understand that model’s behavior if we’re going to use, for example, we have a proprietary anomaly detection model that works in a lot of operational environments. Now, as we’re thinking about some of these newer AI capabilities, which by design are hard to understand how they behave, they’re not fundamentally explainable in the way we’ve thought about even AI or statistical models in the past, and actually their behavior can change over time as they learn and get tuned to new capabilities. That’s really the potential risk of automating a physical system based on capabilities that can evolve over time is one of the things that we have to be really mindful of and really thoughtful around, where are we willing to put some of that increased automation into practice?

But at the same time, I think there’s a real opportunity there, because I glossed over this idea that, okay, well, models evolve, but so do human beings, and sometimes that’s a good thing. We talk about humans having expertise and they gain understanding over their careers of how a system works. If we can actually leverage the ability of some of these newer AI capabilities, these sort of reasoning models often have underlying agentic capabilities, to learn and gather experience faster, and potentially even more importantly or more valuably, take experience that’s learned at one site and apply it to another site, then that’s a real opportunity to take what we already know works for human beings, which is that sometimes you just have to learn by doing and be able to apply that and scale that through AI. That’s where I see potentially a real opportunity in this space.

One of the things that we’re really aware of in the industrial sector is just the way that our workforce is changing. I think that almost half, not quite half, of the industrial workforce is set to retire in the next five years, and that’s a lot of expertise and experience that means that we’re going to lose in the sector. If there’s ways to make sure that we can capture that in ways that are actionable, in ways that can also help a newer generation of workers that are used to experience things in a different way, apply that expertise, apply that knowledge, then I think that’s a huge opportunity within the industrial space.

Megan: Yeah, absolutely. Clearly, some huge opportunities there particularly against the backdrop of other market and workforce changes as you’ve outlined there. I suppose building on that, what is the potential for these autonomous industrial AI systems when built and deployed responsibly to facilitate even faster, more sustainable industrial processes?

Arti: I think there’s a couple different ways to think about this. One is, what are the demands of potentially more environmentally sustainable processes? I’ll use one example of something that my team has been working on in partnership with Idaho National Laboratory here in the U.S. as part of their testing for AI grid resilience project.

One of the challenges in the electric grid as we’re moving toward a future where we have a lot more intermittent renewable power generation sources, often distributed rooftop solar for example, is it’s becoming much more challenging to manage the grid both from really understanding where electric capacity is coming in, electric load is pulling off of the grid. In addition to that, being able to maintain just power quality because instead of having one spinning asset delivering the frequency of electricity that’s going across the grid, you’ve got a lot of smaller systems. AI is actually quite critical for being able to manage that grid of the future. And this is one of the things that we’ve been working in partnership is, how can we do that? How can we help grid operators better understand what’s happening across their system, identify where things might be behaving anomalously so they can detect that early and then remediate for it?

At the same time though, I always talk about that’s an example of where AI can potentially help us accelerate the transition to a lower carbon energy future. At the same time, I think there’s a lot of conversation around the sustainability of AI itself. What are the power requirements? What are the resource requirements needed to run AI? And before I get into how do we think about that at AVEVA, because it is definitely something we think about and I think a lot of actors in the space are thinking about, I want to point out, is one of the challenges is that there’s really no agreed upon method to measure the environmental impact of AI. You see a lot of these stories, like one query on some kind of chat interface is X amount of gallons of water or this amount of electricity use. But the truth is that community-wide, there’s no agreed upon standard.

One of the things that I’m involved with is a standards working group that was launched by the IEEE two years ago, a little over two years ago. I’m the chair of that working group, it’s called the P7100 Standards Working Group on measuring the environmental impact of AI. And one of the things we’re trying to do is really identify all the different areas over which we want to think about environmental sustainability associated with AI, and then having one standard methodology that works and that can be adopted both from a reporting perspective and potentially also from an oversight or regulatory perspective. That becomes really important for any sort of real understanding of how AI impacts the environment is just we have to know, what does it use? We want to look holistically at that. Our standards cover electricity and energy consumption, it covers resource usage, it covers water consumption, and it also covers carbon.

But all of that said, I think it’s important for us to understand the footprint of AI, but I think it’s also important for us to simultaneously recognize that a bigger model uses more compute and more compute probably leverages more resources. The more that we can be intentional and pick the right size model for the right application, the more we can already start down that path of being more environmentally efficient in the AI that we run. One of the potentially nice side effects of that is the more purpose-built a model, the less likely it is to misbehave in unpredictable ways, if you choose correctly your architecture. There’s some sort of ancillary benefits that go beyond environmental sustainability.

Megan: Fascinating. It’s really, really interesting to hear some of the work going on behind the scenes there, because I think we’ll all have heard some of the statistics around the environmental impact, as you say. So, it’s great to understand some of the work going on there to really clarify that.

And we’ve talked a little bit about AI augmenting humans earlier. As systems gain greater autonomy, how should organizations think about that balance between closed loop automation, human in the loop accountability? What guardrails need to be in place? And how are governments and cross-border actors approaching those concerns as well?

Arti: There’s a lot packed into that question, so I’ll try to answer it somewhat one by one. First, starting with that sort of balance between closed loop and human in the loop, automation and accountability. One of the things that we talk about in the industrial sector is from human operator to human supervisor of systems, of industrial systems. And if I’m honest about that, we’re still trying to figure that out. When a human’s in a loop in an automated system, you’re really thinking about a system may process all the data and then make a recommendation.

We’ve got a solution that we’ve been working on more jointly with a few different customers where we’re able to take in a lot of their operational data, also some simulations of how their systems work, and be able to provide, say, recommendations around, you should now operate at this set point instead of that set point based on some of the other conditions that are changing in your plant. There’s a lot of interest in moving from having that be a recommended set point to have an automation that can automatically adjust the set point. And we’ve actually had some successful real-world pilots around that as well.

But when you get into that, obviously it makes people very nervous if you’re changing set points on industrial equipment. That’s where you maybe continue to have some guardrails around like, you can’t go outside of a certain band, for example, of operations, or we only allow the automation in certain areas. That’s where the human supervisor, the same way a human supervisor might give employees a lot of bandwidth or a lot of flexibility to make decisions around certain things, around other things, they’re hard and fast, like this is the deadline or this is the sort of production target. It’s like that. So thinking about, how do you put the appropriate guardrails?

The challenge is, AIs are not human beings, and so the guardrails look different, and I think that’s one of the things that there’s still to think about. That question of, what guardrails should be put in place? I think that it’s going to be probably dependent a little bit on the application, but over time I think we’re all going to learn, and so being really upfront and thoughtful about how we do this I think is important.

But the opportunity though, potentially, is really great. I’ve already mentioned that AI can be very useful in synthesizing a lot of information and bringing to the forefront, this is what matters. That’s something that we do want to create some space to experiment around, but what’s then important is making sure that a human being understands the risk.

I’ll give a little bit of a personal story because it might be illustrative. This weekend, I bought a little toy robot and decided I wanted to program it to do some stuff, and I found AI very, very helpful to get me started to read all the documentation. Putting the robot together was straightforward, they had nice instructions, but there’s a pretty heavy software developer kit that’s already there, but going through and reading all that documentation can take a while. AI was super helpful to help me surface, this is the function that does this, to help me get started. But occasionally, it made really bad recommendations on the best way to troubleshoot something.

That’s where I think having the human being in the loop, being able to say, “I know that it’s not going to be the best software architect or the best troubleshooter,” is really helpful because I had the opportunity to leverage AI for what it’s good for, synthesizing and surfacing a lot of information, but being able to say, “I don’t think that’s the most efficient first step. Let’s try something else.” That’s where it’s a really different way of working, but it’s something that I think as humans get more comfortable with the power and limitations of AI, you can start to teach people how to work with it, and it’s very different from how you would work with other digital tools.

One of the things that is important when it comes to AI is recognizing just the breadth of things that it touches and the breadth of impacts that it’s going to have, whether it’s on the environment, as we’ve discussed, whether it’s on productivity as sort of implicit in this entire discussion, whether it’s on labor force, whether it’s on just how economies work. From my eye, and I’m by no means a policy expert in this area, but from my eye, what I’m seeing is that different governments are prioritizing different aspects of that from how they’re thinking about regulatory and other kind of governance approaches.

Megan: We’re absolutely seeing some really vastly different approaches to this, aren’t we, around the world? I wondered to illustrate some of this, if you could share perhaps some case studies you’ve seen, maybe talking us through what lessons they could hold for other organizations perhaps a little earlier in their own AI journeys.

Arti: I think a lot of the key areas where we’re seeing very clear benefits of adopting AI in the industrial sector, the core to all of them is actually getting the data right and getting the right foundation of data so that you can build AI on top of it.

One of our customers, SCG Chemicals, which is a petrochemical company in Thailand, they had this vision of producing a reliability platform for their operations that was as AI-driven as possible. But a core part of that was actually getting the data right, being able to have all of their information in the right place, leveraging some of AVEVA’s tools to do that. Bringing together operational data and also engineering data. And then putting on top of that AI capabilities, in this case, one of our capabilities called AVEVA Predictive Analytics that deploys some proprietary models to do things like detect anomalies, so that they could really much earlier identify potential operational risks. And instead of having unplanned downtime, translate that to planned downtime. When you translate unplanned downtime to planned downtime, you can get a huge improvement in plant reliability.

At this point they’re targeting something like 99% plant reliability and a very, very high return on investment from the platform that they put in place. Again, in early pilot days, it was almost a 9x ROI, and so that’s really quite impressive. But what I want to emphasize is that it’s kind of a multi-layered problem to get it right.

Megan: Those are some really striking results, though. I mean, for industrial leaders who perhaps are still hesitant to explore AI, I wonder, what do you think is the cost of taking a more wait and see approach?

Arti: I think, again, this is an area where the industrial sector has a little bit of a different calculus to apply to this type of problem. In general, I think you would hear most business experts say that you can’t afford to take a wait and see approach to AI because it is so transformative across every sector of society and economy, and certainly in the industrial space, we’re not immune to that. But I do think that some of the challenges that I’ve outlined today also puts leaders in the industrial space into a mindset of sometimes potentially being a fast follower rather than the first adopter of newer technologies, just because the risk is so high.

But that being said, I think one of the challenges is that the risks that we’ve covered today around infusing systems that don’t always behave predictably with physical systems is that I don’t know that there’s a lot of other sectors that are going to be solving those problems. That’s where what I’m seeing is actually a lot of interest and excitement in trying new things and willingness to do that because there’s a recognition that applied correctly and applied with the right guardrails and safeguards in place, these technologies really have truly transformative potential from a resource usage standpoint, from a human safety standpoint, from a productivity standpoint.

I think the calculus has shifted a little bit in the sector to we want to actually try these things out. But then it becomes more, how do we try these things out in environments that we can make a little bit more sandboxed or safe to test out what some of the unique challenges we’re going to face in the industrial sector are?

Megan: Yeah, absolutely. It’s just hard to ignore the potential nowadays, isn’t it? And just to close with a slightly future forward look, I suppose, what are you most enthusiastic about in terms of the long-term potential of responsible autonomous industrial AI systems?

Arti: Yeah. Well, I think that there’s a couple of different trajectories. One of the things that I think within the next 18 months for sure, we’re going to see an increase of people with deep domain expertise who maybe didn’t grow up with a software background, be able to adopt AI assisted coding techniques to really be able to build the things that they weren’t able to build before.

That’s really exciting in my career, which way back when I was actually an industrial data scientist, I would say I always felt the most energized and that I learned the most talking to the people that were on the front lines of operations, having to monitor a lot of different equipment and understanding how it all worked together. They really have a lot of expertise, and being able to put in their hands the ability to very quickly develop new applications is I think going to really lead to a lot of new ideas that many of us in the industrial software space maybe wouldn’t even have thought about and really understood how to put. I think that’s really exciting.

I think then looking beyond that, I was a little bit of a, not to say a robotic skeptic, because clearly robotics and autonomous systems are going to be important, especially given the types of environments, whether they’re hazardous or remote, that industrial equipment operates in. But I just actually think things are moving a lot faster than I had anticipated. I’m really interested to see how these physical embodiments of AI systems start to really transform, again, how we think about operations.

One of the things about any new technology in any environment is that to really gain value from it, you have to change the way you do things. I would say for close to 10 years now, I’ve been giving talks on AI adoption and I always say the biggest barrier to AI adoption is not anything to do with the technology. It’s not even to do with the data, although data are often the biggest sticking point, it’s really to do with, are you going to change your business processes to be able to work with the way this technology is good or not good at things?

Autonomous systems, whether they’re robots or drones, are really going to change the way that we work in plants, in power systems, on mining sites. And I think that will make these types of operations more efficient, much safer for the human beings involved and more productive. So, I’m quite excited about that.

I don’t know entirely what direction it will go, but one of the things that I think about a lot is that if you go back to I, Robot and Isaac Asimov’s book, the premise of those was that robotics would be the first broadly adopted AI, not computer-based systems. We went in the other direction and I think it’s really interesting to now see all of this converging.

Megan: Yeah, absolutely. See robotics catches up a bit. So many exciting things on the horizon, that’s for sure. Thank you so much, for your time.

That was Arti Garg, chief technologist at AVEVA, whom I spoke with from Brighton in England.

That’s it for this episode of Business Lab. I’m your host, Megan Tatum. I’m a contributing editor at Insights, the custom publishing division of MIT Technology Review. We were founded in 1899 at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, and you can find us in print, on the web, and at events each year around the world. For more information about us and the show, please check out our website at technologyreview.com.

This show is available wherever you get your podcasts. And if you enjoyed us, we hope you’ll take a moment to rate and review us. Business Lab is a production of MIT Technology Review, and this episode was produced by Giro Studios. Thank you so much for listening. Goodbye.

Learn more at aveva.com .

consensus: 工业AI正经历向大模型、物理AI（Physical AI）和智能体（Agentic AI）转型的加速期。
不同于纯软件虚拟环境，工业AI直接干预物理设施，一旦发生错误可能危及人身安全和关键基础设施运行，因此不可预测性是部署的核心痛点。
多源离散数据（遥测、维修日志、工程图纸）的高效整合与关联是工业智能化决策的基础。
现阶段AI应主要扮演辅助与增强人类决策的角色（Augmentation），而非彻底替代核心环节的人类监督。
disagreements: 在工业高风险场景下，自动化自主程度（如机器人独立干预与处置）与严格人工安全屏障（Guardrails/审批流程）之间的权力边界划定与权衡标准在各环节尚无统一共识。
blindSpots: 由于本期内容为与AVEVA赞助合作的企业访谈，叙事高度围绕AVEVA自身技术优势与治理框架展开，缺乏独立第三方评估或质疑视角。

未深入探讨AI在工业企业实际推行中可能引发的一线员工岗位重构、劳动力替代焦虑及转型培训成本等劳工权益议题。

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Huawei doubles down on smartphones as EV sales slow
sourceOnlyStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
sourceOnlyStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: Chinese tech company Huawei wants to rebuild its consumer business after U.S. sanctions halved segment revenue.
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
BEIJING — Faced with a slowdown in the smartphone and car markets, Huawei's consumer business is choosing to focus on phones with homegrown chips.

The Chinese tech giant worked overtime to release its first smartphone — the Mate 90 series — using its own "LogicFolding" chip on Oct. 1, the country's "National Day" and a public holiday,

Ahead of the event, Huawei Executive Director Richard Yu told reporters the company aimed to recover its overseas market share, after U.S. restrictions in 2019 knocked the China-based company from a brief first place. Yu said that at the time, Huawei shipped more than 240 million smartphones in China and elsewhere — with a goal of 300 million units in 2019.

But now Huawei only sells several million smartphones outside China each year, Yu said. He added the company plans to expand its HarmonyOS operating system to overseas markets in the next one to three years, and hopes China's chip manufacturing capacity will one day enable overseas sales of devices with self-developed chips.

Yu, chairman of Huawei's consumer business, has long been the on-stage presenter for the company's smartphone and car events.

The media roundtable ahead of the Mate 90 series launch marked Yu's first time speaking with foreign press since 2019. That year, U.S. restrictions blocked Huawei's access to Google's Android operating system and TSMC-made semiconductors.

As the impact of the sanctions kicked in, Huawei's consumer business — once the company's largest by revenue — halved to about $34 billion in 2021 from the year before. Since then, the consumer business has grown to around $51 billion in 2025, or 39% of total revenue, according to CNBC calculations.

Huawei's push into the smartphone market comes as sales in China have slumped this year, with a double-digit decline year-on-year in August and September, according to Counterpoint Research.

Meanwhile, Huawei got into the electric car business by working with several Chinese car manufacturers, and has built a business unit with revenues of at least $6.7 billion in 2025, according to the tech giant's annual report. Unlike other Chinese electric cars' rapid growth in exports, the Huawei-powered vehicles are so far concentrated in China. Huawei has emphasized it does not manufacture the cars, but provides the software interface and driver-assist system.

But China's auto market is on track for its worst year since 2021, with sales down by more than 20% over roughly the first three quarters of the year, according to China Passenger Car Association data as of Sept. 27. New energy vehicles, which include battery electric and hybrid-powered cars, have seen sales tumble 13% during that time, the data showed.

In September, Huawei-powered vehicles saw deliveries drop for a third-straight month, down by 29% from a year ago, according to CNBC calculations of publicly available figures from Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance, or HIMA, Huawei's auto tech software system.

That contrasted with double-digit gains for market leader BYD in each of the past three months, with sales well above 400,000 units a month, company data showed. Leapmotor, meanwhile, maintained rapid growth, with deliveries topping 100,000 cars a month since July.

HIMA, whose five lines of vehicles reflect partnerships with manufacturers such as Chery and Seres, in contrast delivered just under 37,500 vehicles in September. More than 1.56 million units were sold since the first Huawei-powered car was launched in late 2021. Tesla China had yet to report September deliveries as of Wednesday afternoon.

In December 2021, Yu showed off the first car with Huawei's tech installed, the Aito M5.

But Seres Group, which makes the Aito EV line, has seen its Shanghai-listed shares drop by more than 60% so far this year.

On Oct. 1, Huawei announced it had signed with Seres to cooperate for another five years, including the joint establishment of an Aito business team. Mainland China markets are set to reopen Thursday after being closed since Oct. 1.

sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
Operation on 19-year-old who had no sperm after chemotherapy offers hope of preserving children’s fertility after cancer treatment

Surgeons have performed the first testicular tissue transplant on a teenager in the UK, offering hope that boys left infertile by chemotherapy could one day have biological children.

The 19-year-old had his tissue removed and frozen three years ago before undergoing treatment for a serious blood disorder. He said he was “incredibly grateful” to the medical team behind the pioneering procedure, which represents a potential breakthrough for male fertility preservation.

worldStories.title: Yandex数据中心起火、399架无人机来袭：俄多地遭袭后果通报
worldStories.originalTitle: Fire at Yandex data center, 399 UAVs: aftermath of attacks on Russian regions
worldStories.snippet: According to Russian Defense Ministry, Ukrainian drones were downed over 21 Russian regions
worldStories.fullContent:
MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 399 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the Black Sea overnight, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.

A drone attack caused a fire at a data center operated by Russia’s tech giant Yandex in the town of Sasovo in the country’s central Ryazan Region, damaging part of the facility’s infrastructure.

Drone debris fell on the territory of an enterprise in Russia’s southern city of Krasnodar, causing a fire.

A fire also broke out in the industrial zone in the city of Salavat in Russia’s central Bashkortostan Region as a result of falling drone debris after an attack was repelled.

TASS has compiled the main details about the aftermath.

- On-duty air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 399 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over Russian regions between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 p.m. GMT) on October 7 and 8:00 a.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. GMT) on October 8, the Defense Ministry reported.

- According to the ministry, drones were downed over the Belgorod, Bryansk, Volgograd, Voronezh, Kursk, Lipetsk, Oryol, Orenburg, Penza, Rostov, Ryazan, Samara, Saratov, Smolensk, Tambov, Tula, Ulyanovsk, Moscow, Bashkortostan and Tatarstan Regions, the Republic of Crimea and the waters of the Black Sea.

- More than 30 UAVs were destroyed overnight over the town of Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, the Kamensky, Millerovsky, Neklinovsky, Chertkovsky and Sholokhovsky Districts of the Rostov Region, Governor Yury Slyusar said on his Max channel.

- Air defense systems shot down 26 Ukrainian drones over the Voronezh Region overnight, Governor Alexander Gusev wrote in a post on his Max channel.

- Air defense forces intercepted two drones over the Ryazan Region overnight, Governor Pavel Malkov said on his Max channel.

- A drone attack caused a fire at a data center operated by Russia’s tech giant Yandex in the town of Sasovo in the Ryazan Region, damaging part of the facility’s infrastructure, the company’s press service told TASS.

- There were no casualties, with special services carrying out cleanup operations on site.

- The data center’s operations have been fully suspended, and some Yandex services may be unavailable to users.

- Earlier, the Yandex Cloud Telegram channel, used to promptly notify users about service outages and their recovery, reported that power supply issues were affecting the ru-central1-b availability zone.

- The company said that as of 8:26 a.m. Moscow time (5:26 a.m. GMT), the ru-central1-b zone was still unavailable, while all necessary work to transfer the load to other availability zones had been completed.

- Creating new resources in the cloud infrastructure may currently be limited, with specialists still working to address the consequences of the incident.

- All services in other zones are running normally.

- A drone attack caused a fire on the roof of an enterprise in the Sasovsky District of the Ryazan Region, Governor Pavel Malkov reported on his Max channel.

- Windows were also shattered in several private houses.

- There have been no casualties reported so far.

- Emergency services are operating on site.

- A fire broke out in the industrial zone in the city of Salavat in the Bashkortostan Region as a result of falling UAV debris after an attack was repelled, Mayor Marat Zagidullin said on his Max channel.

- Emergency services are working on site.

- The affected enterprise remains operational.

- There were no casualties.

- Drone debris fell on the territory of an enterprise in the city of Krasnodar, the regional emergency response center reported on its Telegram channel.

- Drone fragments damaged the facility and sparked a fire, which was promptly extinguished.

- Emergency and special services are working on site.

- As a result of a Ukrainian drone attack, several settlements have been left without power in western and central Crimea, the Krymenergo state company said on its Max channel.

- Restrictions on electricity consumption are currently in place in Crimea.

- Power lines or grid equipment are promptly shut down when necessary in the energy districts to carry out repair work.

- The timelines for restoring electricity supply currently depend on the stability of the situation and the possibility of conducting repairs safely.

- Due to technological disruptions at a facility of the Tavricheskoye Main Power Grid Enterprise, the Bakhchisaraysky District is facing a difficult electricity supply situation.

- Several settlements have restricted electricity supply.

- Backup power supply schemes are being used.

- Emergency repair crews are working around the clock.

- A man born in 1981 was injured in an overnight drone attack on the Kirovsky District in the city of Donetsk, Alexey Kulemzin, municipal head, said on his Telegram channel.

- The injured man was taken to hospital.

- Windows of a private house were also damaged.

- In the Kalininsky District of the city of Gorlovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR), two passenger buses were damaged, Ivan Prikhodko, city district head, wrote on Telegram.

- The published photos show the driver-side windshields shattered in both vehicles.

- The buses were operating on routes No. 2 and No. 19.

塔斯社莫斯科10月8日电 俄罗斯国防部通报称，防空系统夜间在俄罗斯多个地区及黑海上空拦截并摧毁了399架乌克兰无人机。

一架无人机袭击引发了俄罗斯科技巨头Yandex位于俄中部梁赞州萨索沃镇的数据中心火灾，损坏了该设施的部分基础设施。

无人机残骸坠落在俄罗斯南部城市克拉斯诺达尔一家企业的厂区内并引发火灾。

在俄中部巴什科尔托斯坦共和国萨拉瓦特市，一次袭击被击退后，坠落的无人机残骸导致当地工业园区起火。

塔斯社汇总了有关此次袭击后果的主要细节：

- 国防部通报，莫斯科时间10月7日晚上8:00（格林尼治标准时间下午5:00）至10月8日早上8:00（格林尼治标准时间凌晨5:00）期间，值班防空系统在俄罗斯多个地区上空拦截并摧毁了399架乌克兰固定翼无人机（UAV）。

- 国防部表示，被击落无人机分布在别尔哥罗德州、布良斯克州、伏尔加格勒州、沃罗涅日州、库尔斯克州、利佩茨克州、奥廖尔州、奥伦堡州、奔萨州、罗斯托夫州、梁赞州、萨马拉州、萨拉托夫州、斯摩棱斯克州、坦波夫州、图拉州、乌里扬诺夫斯克州、莫斯科州、巴什科尔托斯坦共和国、鞑靼斯坦共和国、克里米亚共和国以及黑海海域上空。

- 罗斯托夫州州长尤里·斯柳萨尔在其Max频道上表示，夜间在卡缅斯克-沙赫京斯基市以及该州的卡缅斯克区、米列罗沃区、涅克利诺夫卡区、切尔特科沃区和绍洛霍夫区上空摧毁了30多架无人机。

- 沃罗涅日州州长亚历山大·古谢夫在其Max频道发文称，防空系统夜间在该州上空击落了26架乌克兰无人机。

- 梁赞州州长帕维尔·马尔科夫在其Max频道上表示，防空部队夜间在该州上空拦截了两架无人机。

- 俄罗斯科技巨头Yandex新闻处向塔斯社透露，无人机袭击引发了该公司位于梁赞州萨索沃镇的数据中心火灾，损坏了该设施的部分基础设施。

- 现场无人员伤亡，特种部门正在现场开展善后清理工作。

- 该数据中心的运营已全面暂停，部分Yandex服务可能对用户不可用。

- 早些时候，用于及时向用户通报服务中断及恢复情况的Yandex Cloud Telegram频道曾发布消息称，供电问题影响到了ru-central1-b可用区。

- 该公司表示，截至莫斯科时间早上8:26（格林尼治标准时间凌晨5:26），ru-central1-b区仍不可用，而将负载转移到其他可用区的所有必要工作均已完成。

- 云基础设施中创建新资源的功能目前可能会受到限制，专业人员仍在致力于消除该事件造成的影响。

- 其他区域的所有服务均运行正常。

- 梁赞州州长帕维尔·马尔科夫在其Max频道上报告称，无人机袭击导致该州萨索沃区一家企业的屋顶起火。

- 几座私人住宅的窗户也被震碎。

- 迄今暂无人员伤亡报告。

- 紧急救援部门正在现场作业。

- 萨拉瓦特市市长马拉特·扎吉杜林在其Max频道上表示，袭击被击退后，坠落的无人机残骸导致巴什科尔托斯坦共和国萨拉瓦特市工业园区发生火灾。

- 紧急救援部门正在现场开展工作。

- 受波及的企业仍维持正常运转。

- 无人员伤亡。

- 克拉斯诺达尔边疆区应急响应中心在其Telegram频道上报告称，无人机残骸坠落在克拉斯诺达尔市一家企业的厂区内。

- 无人机碎片损毁了该设施并引发火灾，火势被迅速扑灭。

- 紧急救援部门和特种部门正在现场开展工作。

- 克里米亚国家电力公司（Krymenergo）在其Max频道上表示，由于乌克兰无人机袭击，克里米亚西部和中部的数个定居点发生停电。

- 目前克里米亚正在实施用电限制。

- 必要时，能源区域内的输电线路或电网设备将迅速关停以进行抢修。

- 恢复供电的时间表目前取决于局势的稳定程度以及安全开展维修作业的可能性。

- 由于塔夫里切斯科耶主要电网企业的一处设施发生技术故障，巴赫奇萨赖区正面临严峻的供电形势。

- 几个定居点的供电受到限制。

- 目前正在启用备用供电方案。

- 紧急抢修队伍正在全天候作业。

- 顿涅茨克市市长阿列克谢·库列姆津在其Telegram频道上表示，一名1981年出生的男子在顿涅茨克市基洛夫区夜间遭无人机袭击时受伤。

- 该伤者已被送往医院。

- 一处私人住宅的窗户也遭到损坏。

- 顿涅茨克人民共和国（DPR）戈尔洛夫卡市加里宁区区长伊万·普里霍季科在Telegram上发文称，两辆客运公交车受损。

- 公布的照片显示，两辆车的驾驶员一侧挡风玻璃均已破碎。

- 这两辆公交车当时分别在2号线和19号线上运营。

无人机被击落的区域包括别尔哥罗德、布良斯克、伏尔加格勒、沃罗涅日、库尔斯克、利佩茨克、奥廖尔、奥伦堡、奔萨、罗斯托夫、梁赞、萨马拉、萨拉托夫、斯摩棱斯克、坦波夫、图拉、乌里扬诺夫斯克、莫斯科、巴什科尔托斯坦和鞑靼斯坦等地区，以及克里米亚共和国和黑海海域。
梁赞州萨索沃镇的Yandex数据中心遭遇无人机袭击引发火灾，部分基础设施受损，无人员伤亡，该数据中心已全面暂停运营。
Yandex Cloud的ru-central1-b可用区供电受影响且截至莫斯科时间8:26仍不可用，负载转移至其他可用区的工作已完成，其他区域服务正常运行。
梁赞州萨索夫斯基区一家企业屋顶因无人机袭击起火，数座民房窗户破损，暂无伤亡报告。
无人机残骸坠落导致克拉斯诺达尔市一家企业起火，火势已被迅速扑灭。
无人机袭击被击退后残骸坠落，导致巴什科尔托斯坦共和国萨拉瓦特市工业区起火，无人员伤亡，受影响企业维持运转。
罗斯托夫州卡缅斯克-沙赫京斯基市及多个区上空夜间摧毁了30多架无人机。
沃罗涅日州上空夜间击落26架乌克兰无人机。
梁赞州上空夜间拦截了2架无人机。
无人机袭击导致克里米亚西部和中部数个定居点断电，巴赫奇萨赖区面临电力供应困难，实行限电措施并启用备用供电方案。
顿涅茨克市基洛夫斯基区夜间无人机袭击导致一名1981年出生的男子受伤送医，一座民房窗户受损。
戈尔洛夫卡市加里宁斯基区两辆载客公交车（2路和19路）受损，驾驶侧挡风玻璃破碎。

evidence.quote: On-duty air defense systems intercepted and destroyed 399 Ukrainian fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) over Russian regions between 8:00 p.m. Moscow time (5:00 p.m. GMT) on October 7 and 8:00 a.m. Moscow time (5:00 a.m. GMT) on October 8, the Defense Ministry reported.

A drone attack caused a fire at a data center operated by Russia’s tech giant Yandex in the town of Sasovo in the Ryazan Region, damaging part of the facility’s infrastructure, the company’s press service told TASS.
The data center’s operations have been fully suspended, and some Yandex services may be unavailable to users.
Drone debris fell on the territory of an enterprise in the city of Krasnodar, the regional emergency response center reported on its Telegram channel.

A fire broke out in the industrial zone in the city of Salavat in the Bashkortostan Region as a result of falling UAV debris after an attack was repelled, Mayor Marat Zagidullin said on his Max channel.
As a result of a Ukrainian drone attack, several settlements have been left without power in western and central Crimea, the Krymenergo state company said on its Max channel.
A man born in 1981 was injured in an overnight drone attack on the Kirovsky District in the city of Donetsk, Alexey Kulemzin, municipal head, said on his Telegram channel.

position.sourceRole: 俄方通讯社英文报道，主要汇编俄罗斯国防部、地方官员、企业和应急机构对无人机拦截、设施受损及人员伤亡情况的通报；文中所述关键事实多为俄方机构或地方政府单方面发布，部分信息未经独立第三方核实。
position.narrativeFocus: 聚焦俄罗斯多个地区及黑海上空大规模无人机拦截的后果，突出俄国防部所称“拦截并摧毁399架无人机”，以及梁赞州Yandex数据中心起火停运、克里米亚部分地区断电、俄境内企业和民用设施受损、顿涅茨克和戈尔洛夫卡出现人员及交通设施损失等情况。报道主要采用俄方官方口径，将事件框定为乌克兰无人机袭击及其在俄控制或管辖地区造成的影响。
stakeholders: 俄罗斯国防部
俄罗斯各受影响地区的州长、市长和地方行政机构
Yandex及Yandex Cloud
Krymenergo等能源和基础设施运营方
俄罗斯应急和特种服务部门
俄罗斯居民、企业及公共交通使用者
乌克兰及其相关军事部门
受影响地区的地方居民与伤者
consensus: 报道所述期间，俄方机构报告多个地区发生无人机拦截、坠落或相关火灾及基础设施扰动。
Yandex数据中心、部分企业、住宅窗户、供电设施和公交车辆据报道受到不同程度影响。
俄方通报称多数相关事件没有造成人员伤亡，但顿涅茨克市报告一人受伤。
Yandex方面报告梁赞州数据中心部分基础设施受损、相关可用区暂时不可用，其他可用区服务正常。
disagreements: 文中称无人机为“乌克兰无人机”并将事件归因于乌克兰袭击，但证据包显示乌克兰方面是否发动或确认袭击未获独立第三方核实。
399架无人机被拦截或摧毁、各地区具体击落数量及损害规模均主要来自俄罗斯国防部或地方官员，缺少乌方、独立调查机构或现场核查材料的交叉验证。
报道将无人机残骸引发的火灾、停电和设施损坏与袭击直接关联，但没有提供独立技术鉴定以确认损害原因。
blindSpots: 没有乌克兰政府、军方或其他乌方来源的回应，也没有说明乌方是否承认相关行动或目标。
没有独立卫星图像、现场影像、航空追踪或第三方调查来核实无人机数量、拦截成功率及损害范围。
未说明所谓“拦截并摧毁”399架无人机的统计口径、证据依据，以及是否可能包含重复计数或仅据雷达判断。
对无人机袭击的军事背景、目标选择、发射地点和战略意图没有展开分析。
克里米亚断电的具体受损设备、影响人口、恢复进度和最终停电时长尚不明确。
对Yandex数据中心停运造成的服务影响、数据安全、业务损失及恢复情况报道有限。
报道未系统区分俄罗斯国际承认边界内地区、克里米亚及顿涅茨克和戈尔洛夫卡等争议地区的法律与政治地位。

worldStories.title: 顶级保守派团体在关键摇摆州展开全方位攻势，揭露民主党“令人震惊”的政策纲领
worldStories.originalTitle: Top conservative group unveils full-court press in key battleground state to expose ‘shocking’ Dem platform
worldStories.snippet: Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America has knocked on over 172,000 doors in Iowa, saying voters are shocked by the Democratic Party's abortion stance.
worldStories.fullContent:
FIRST ON FOX - CEDAR RAPIDS, IA : One of the largest pro-life organizations in the country is pouring time and resources into the high-stakes battleground of Iowa, making the case that voters of all backgrounds will be "shocked" to know where the Democratic Party stands on abortion.

Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America’s ground game has knocked on over 172,000 doors in Iowa promoting the Republican ticket in the Hawkeye State. Additionally, the group has a planned digital spend of $650,000 to go along with a $1.35 million spend from the Women Speak Out PAC, SBA’s super PAC, to contact voters in the Iowa universe.

"The scale of SBA Pro-Life America’s voter contact program is among the largest in the nation and certainly the largest in the pro-life movement," SBA President Marjorie Dannenfelser told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital was on the ground in Iowa with SBA canvassers in Cedar Rapids on Tuesday, where the team passed out flyers and spoke to voters in support of Iowa Republican Sen. Ashley Hinson and hammered the abortion positions of Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand.

TRUMP-ENDORSED HINSON SECURES IOWA SENATE NOMINATION AS DEMOCRATS EYE GOP SEAT

"Our goal really is just to inform voters," SBA field rep Amy Elizabeth told Fox News Digital. "Most people we're finding are pro-life, regardless of the way that they vote and we want to make sure that they're aware of the candidate's views on abortion and pro-life and we wanna make sure they're making knowledgeable and informed decisions when they go to the polls."

Literature passed out by the canvassers calls Sand "wrong for Iowa families" while arguing that he will "do everything in his power to overturn Governor Kim Reynolds’ pro-life legacy" and "even supports painful late term abortions . The literature also promotes Hinson as the "pro-life champion" that Iowans "need in DC."

Elizabeth told Fox News Digital that the conversations with voters on the ground have been effective.

"Some of my favorite conversations have come from people who normally wouldn't vote the same way that I would vote," Elizabeth explained. "They're not typically conservative voters. They are a little bit more liberal leaning. But when we really are open to having conversations together and I can share with them some information about the candidates that they typically would vote for, they are very surprised and they're very shocked to hear how those candidates feel on some issues that are important to them."

NEW MIDTERM BATTLEGROUND TAKES SHAPE AS PARTIES BUILD ELECTION ARMIES

Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America and Women Speak Out PAC announced in August that their Iowa voter-contact program had surpassed 100,000 visits to voters’ homes in the Des Moines, Davenport and Cedar Rapids areas. The groups said the effort is targeting persuadable and low-turnout voters ahead of November’s elections, with the goal of defeating Democrats they describe as "pro-abortion" and electing candidates who support abortion restrictions.

Nationwide, Dannenfelser says SBA will ultimately reach 10.5 million voters during this election cycle, including 4 million at their front doors in person.

"Our hardworking field team has been on the ground in key battleground states, educating voters about the Democrats’ radical agenda of all-trimester abortion -- anytime, for any reason, paid for by taxpayers -- even when babies can feel pain," Dannenfelser said.

"Polling shows the vast majority of Americans reject this, and our team at the doors is finding it true visit after visit. One conversation at a time, we are changing hearts, minds, and votes. We focus on Republicans, Democrats, and Independents that can be persuaded and low-propensity, pro-life voters. All these groups are shocked by Democrats’ extremism on abortion."

A third of Republicans would be less likely to vote in the midterms if they believe that the GOP has abandoned the abortion issue, according to polling released earlier this year, suggesting that driving pro-life Republicans to vote will play an important role in the party's hopes to retain control of Congress in November.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
福克斯新闻独家报道——爱荷华州锡达拉皮兹：全美最大的反堕胎组织之一正在向关键摇摆州爱荷华州投入大量时间和资源，他们主张，任何背景的选民在了解民主党在堕胎问题上的立场后，都会感到“震惊”。

“苏珊·B·安东尼反堕胎美国组织”（Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America，简称SBA）的地面行动已在“鹰眼州”（爱荷华州）敲响了超过17.2万户家庭的大门，为共和党候选人团队助选。此外，该组织计划投入65万美元的数字广告费用，并结合SBA旗下的超级政治行动委员会“女性发声PAC”（Women Speak Out PAC）投入的135万美元，用以接触爱荷华州的选民群体。

SBA总裁玛乔丽·丹嫩费尔瑟（Marjorie Dannenfelser）在接受福克斯数字新闻采访时表示：“SBA反堕胎美国组织的选民联络项目规模在全美名列前茅，在反堕胎运动中更无疑是规模最大的。”

周二，福克斯数字新闻记者在锡达拉皮兹与SBA的入户游说员一起深入爱荷华州基层。团队成员在此派发传单，与选民交谈以支持爱荷华州共和党籍参议员阿什莉·辛森（Ashley Hinson），并抨击民主党籍州长候选人罗伯·桑德（Rob Sand）的堕胎立场。

【相关阅读：获特朗普背书的辛森锁定爱荷华州参议员提名，民主党瞄准共和党席位】

“我们真正的目标只是向选民传递信息，”SBA一线外勤代表艾米·伊丽莎白（Amy Elizabeth）告诉福克斯数字新闻，“我们发现，无论人们平时如何投票，大多数人骨子里其实都是反堕胎的。我们希望确保他们了解候选人对堕胎和反堕胎的看法，并确保他们在走进投票站时能做出明智且知情的决定。”

游说人员派发的宣传资料称桑德“不适合爱荷华州的家庭”，指责他将“竭尽全力推翻州长金·雷诺兹（Kim Reynolds）的反堕胎政治遗产”，并“甚至支持痛苦的晚期堕胎”。宣传册还宣传辛森是爱荷华州人在华盛顿特区“所需要的反堕胎捍卫者”。

伊丽莎白告诉福克斯数字新闻，基层与选民的面对面沟通非常有效。

“我最喜欢的一些交流，正是来自于那些通常投票意向和我完全不同的人，”伊丽莎白解释道，“他们并非典型的保守派选民，往往略偏自由派。但当我们真正坦诚交谈，由我向他们透露一些他们通常支持的候选人的真实信息时，他们听到那些候选人在一些关键问题上的立场，感到非常意外和震惊。”

【相关阅读：随着各党派组建竞选大军，新的中期选举战场逐渐成形】

“苏珊·B·安东尼反堕胎美国组织”与“女性发声PAC”在8月宣布，他们在德梅因、达文波特和锡达拉皮兹等地区的爱荷华州选民联络项目已突破10万次敲门家访。这些团体表示，该行动旨在11月大选前锁定可被说服的选民以及投票率较低的选民，目标是击败被他们称作“支持堕胎”的民主党人，选出支持限制堕胎的候选人。

丹嫩费尔瑟表示，在整个竞选周期中，SBA最终将在全美范围内接触1050万名选民，其中有400万人将通过面对面敲门家访的形式进行接触。

丹嫩费尔瑟说：“我们辛勤的外勤团队已进驻关键摇摆州，向选民揭露民主党在堕胎问题上的激进议程——即全孕期均可堕胎、随时随地、因任何理由、且由纳税人买单——甚至在胎儿已经能感受到疼痛时也是如此。”

“民调显示绝大多数美国人拒绝接受这种做法，我们敲门的团队在一次又一次的走访中印证了这一点。通过一次又一次的对话，我们正在改变人们的心态、观念和选票。我们的重点是可以被说服的共和党人、民主党人和独立选民，以及投票意愿低但反堕胎的选民。所有这些群体都对民主党在堕胎问题上的极端主义感到震惊。”

今年早些时候公布的一项民调显示，如果共和党选民认为该党放弃了堕胎议题，三分之一的人在中期选举中投票的可能性会降低。这表明，动员反堕胎的共和党选民出门投票，将对该党在11月保住国会控制权的希望起到至关重要的作用。

worldStories.originalTitle: America’s multi-billion tech boom comes into focus as 7 key states put it to a midterm test
worldStories.snippet: Voters across eight states will decide 34 data center ballot measures this November as America's AI boom becomes a growing political flashpoint.
worldStories.fullContent:
The rapid buildout of data centers powering America’s artificial intelligence (AI) boom is heading to the ballot box this November, as voters across the country weigh measures that could shape where and how the massive facilities are built.

Voters will decide 34 data center-related ballot measures across seven states — California, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Nevada, Ohio and Wisconsin.

The measures come as states elsewhere have considered or imposed limits on development, underscoring how quickly data centers have become a political flashpoint.

A Fox News national poll conducted last month found voters struggling to reconcile AI’s potential benefits with the economic and environmental costs of the data centers that power the technology.

8 EVERYDAY THINGS THAT WOULD QUIT WORKING WITHOUT DATA CENTERS

More than seven in 10 voters (71%) opposed building AI data centers in their area, including 46% who strongly opposed them. More than half (52%) supported building them in remote locations, while 44% opposed.

Overall, 60% of voters had a negative view of AI, compared with 37% who viewed it positively. That 23-point gap has more than doubled since a July Fox News poll .

The Fox News poll also found a partisan divide over AI and data centers. Voters with favorable views of AI leaned Republican, while those with unfavorable views leaned Democratic.

The divide was even sharper over data centers, with Republicans performing better among voters who supported them and Democrats among those who opposed them.

That partisan split comes as AI policy emerges as a growing fault line in Washington and on the campaign trail.

AI IS SUPERCHARGING POLITICAL AD WARS. BUT VIRAL DOESN’T MEAN VICTORIOUS

President Donald Trump has opposed wide-ranging federal regulation of the AI industry and warned that the U.S. cannot allow China to win the technology race.

But as the midterms approach, the debate over AI and the data centers powering it is playing out in races across the country.

In Texas, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott , who previously courted major tech investments, recently ordered a pause on data center permitting and grid connections pending an audit. Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa has supported temporary moratoriums.

‘BACKWARDS AND POOR’: TRUMP SLAMS COMMUNITIES BLOCKING DATA CENTERS

Meanwhile, in the state’s Senate race, Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic state Rep. James Talarico have battled over tax breaks for the industry.

In Ohio, the debate is playing out both on the campaign trail and at the ballot box. The state has 20 data center-related measures across 17 jurisdictions this November — more than any other state and more than half of the 34 measures going before voters nationwide.

Democratic Senate challenger Sherrod Brown has attacked Republican Sen. Jon Husted over data center development. Trump, campaigning for Husted, defended the industry’s economic potential.

"Look, there’s so much money to be made for Ohio, you can’t just turn them off," Trump said.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
为美国人工智能（AI）热潮提供动力的庞大数据中心正在迅速扩张，而这一议题即将在今年11月交由选民裁决。全美各地的选民将对相关公投提案进行权衡，这些提案可能会重塑这些庞大设施的选址和建设方式。

选民将在7个州——加利福尼亚州、佛罗里达州、伊利诺伊州、堪萨斯州、内华达州、俄亥俄州和威斯康星州——就34项与数据中心相关的公投提案做出表决。

与此同时，其他各州也已在考虑或实施对开发项目的限制措施，这突显出数据中心已迅速成为一个政治焦点。

福克斯新闻（Fox News）上个月进行的一项全美民调发现，选民们正努力在人工智能的潜在益处与支撑该技术的数据中心所带来的经济和环境成本之间寻求平衡。

若没有数据中心就将停止运作的8种日常事物

超过七成选民（71%）反对在自己所在地区建设人工智能数据中心，其中包括46%的人表示强烈反对。超过半数（52%）的人支持在偏远地区建设，而44%的人表示反对。

总体而言，60%的选民对人工智能持负面看法，相比之下持积极看法的仅占37%。自7月份福克斯新闻民调以来，这一23个百分点的差距扩大了一倍以上。

福克斯新闻的民调还发现，在人工智能和数据中心问题上存在党派分歧。对人工智能持好感的选民倾向于共和党，而持反感态度的选民则倾向于民主党。

在数据中心问题上的分歧更为显著：共和党在支持数据中心的选民中表现更好，而民主党在反对数据中心的选民中表现更佳。

这种党派分歧出现之际，人工智能政策正在华盛顿以及竞选活动中演变为日益扩大的政治分歧点。

人工智能正在加剧政治广告战，但引发病毒式传播并不意味着获胜

唐纳德·特朗普总统反对联邦层面对人工智能行业实施广泛的监管，并警告称美国不能让中国赢得科技竞赛。

但随着中期选举临近，有关人工智能及支撑它运转的数据中心的争论正在全美各地的竞选中上演。

在得克萨斯州，此前曾积极争取大型科技投资的共和党籍州长格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）最近下令，在审计完成之前暂停数据中心审批和电网并网许可。民主党挑战者吉娜·伊诺霍萨（Gina Hinojosa）则支持实施临时暂停令。

“落后且贫困”：特朗普抨击阻挠数据中心建设的社区

与此同时，在该州的参议院竞选中，共和党籍总检察长肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）与民主党籍州众议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科（James Talarico）就针对该行业的税收减免展开了交锋。

在俄亥俄州，争论正在竞选过程和投票站同时展开。今年11月，该州17个辖区共有20项与数据中心相关的公投提案——这一数量超过其他任何州，且占到全美选民面前34项提案的半数以上。

民主党籍参议院挑战者谢罗德·布朗（Sherrod Brown）就数据中心开发问题抨击了共和党籍参议员乔恩·赫斯特德（Jon Husted）。而为赫斯特德助选的特朗普则捍卫了该行业的经济潜力。

特朗普表示：“听着，俄亥俄州有大笔钱可赚，你不能直接把它们关停。”

worldStories.snippet: Trump ended catch-and-release at the border, but Ceuta's mass migrant rush shows why demand-side migration pressures still threaten the U.S.
worldStories.fullContent:
Retired Chief Border Patrol agent Chris Clem discusses a caravan of more than 600 migrants traveling from Honduras through Mexico toward the U.S.

Back in August 2023, hundreds of foreign nationals rushed the U.S. border in separate incidents at official crossing points in Brownsville and El Paso, Texas. DHS officers put up physical barriers and stopped traffic over the Gateway International Bridge. On the Mexican side, the military intervened to stop further mass attempts by aliens to enter the U.S. illegally.

For those who have already forgotten, we very recently had hundreds of thousands of inadmissible aliens pouring over our border every month. Why did they come in the millions from 2021-2024 and only a few hundred today? Policy choices. Former President Joe Biden and his Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas were lamentably successful at creating made-up "lawful pathways" and circumventing our laws to parole or release as many aliens into our country as possible. The effects will last decades.

We saw an echo of the Biden border recently in the Spanish city of Ceuta, in North Africa. In July, more than 72,000 non-Spaniards bum-rushed the border while Morocco did little to stop them. The majority were Moroccans, who mostly went home within a few days. But 10,000 or more were from sub-Saharan Africa or claimed to be minors, or both.

SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD

Spain is now stuck with processing them under Europe’s insanely soft asylum policies, which will likely result in many being taken to mainland Spain. The success of even a minority of these invaders to access Europe will encourage many more to try.

Escorted by the Spanish army, migrants who crossed into Spain return to Morocco from the Spanish enclave of Ceuta on Saturday, Aug. 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)

President Donald Trump ended Biden’s open-borders policies. Since he took office, there have been zero "catch-and-release" cases at the border, the Department of Homeland Security says. Trump also ended Biden’s reckless and illegal mass parole programs. Some aliens still sneak in without being caught, but far fewer now that the Border Patrol has the time and manpower to look for them and the mandate to detain them.

TRUMP ADMIN MARKS 15 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH ZERO BORDER RELEASES AS APPREHENSIONS PLUNGE 94%

Trump’s prompt action stemmed the manmade disaster that allowed up to 10 million illegal aliens into our country with no vetting and little chance of qualifying for asylum. But Trump can’t change the demand-side of the mass migration equation. The world still has plenty of poor, dysfunctional countries.

True, there have been some success stories. Elections across Latin America including Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, and Peru have replaced leftist leaders with conservative ones, which augers well for security and prosperity in our hemisphere.

TANVI RATNA: LATIN AMERICA'S RIGHT TURN IS REDRAWING THE UNITED STATES' BACKYARD

In El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has drastically reduced crime and improved the economy such that the country is desperate for workers. The U.S. taking out Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and replacing him with a more cooperative, if still leftist, leader should improve that country’s economy and allow millions to return home safely.

But elsewhere in Latin America, Africa and Asia, bad governments, weak economies, and high fertility continue to make people want to leave. The U.S. remains a favored destination.

So does Europe, where the native population is slowly being supplanted by mass migration from the "Global South." This is no conspiracy theory; it’s an observable demographic phenomenon.

The U.N. High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) estimated that at least 1,200 migrants in Ceuta could be eligible for asylum in Spain. UNHCR, along with the International Organization for Migration, used millions in U.S. money to channel illegal migration from across the world via Latin America into the U.S.

MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

Claiming asylum so they can get into Spain and the larger EU is what motivates people rushing into Ceuta, just like those who used to rush the U.S. border. They want jobs and better prospects, including generous welfare benefits. But the vast majority are not persecuted at home in the way required to qualify for asylum. They’ll admit as much themselves, at least until the asylum process begins and they have to make up a story and stick to it.

President Donald Trump ended Biden’s open-borders policies. Since he took office, there have been zero "catch-and-release" cases at the border, the Department of Homeland Security says. Trump also ended Biden’s reckless and illegal mass parole programs.

One illegal migrant to Ceuta from Chad, Mohamed Yaqoub, told an AP reporter that "The most important thing for us is to get the papers," so that he could achieve his goal of studying in France. If he were truly seeking asylum, Yaqoub would have done so in the first safe country he reached outside Chad. He not only didn’t, he admits he won’t even stay in Spain once he gets "papers," he’ll go to France.

THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS REMAIN IN SPANISH TERRITORY AFTER BORDER RUSH, DEATH TOLL HITS ABOUT 100: CEUTA OFFICIAL

Demand to migrate from the Global South to the richer countries is insatiable. But housing, healthcare and welfare benefits are limited. Many EU member countries have structural budget deficits and debt caused by their economies failing to grow while the costs of socialist healthcare and pension systems rise.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The United States is largely in the same boat. Now, like Europe, we have evidence that the typical illegal or low-skilled legal migrant results in a net fiscal loss over his lifetime – thus not saving Social Security, but sinking it.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Let Ceuta and Brownsville, be a warning to us to never let the Biden border happen again.

Simon Hankinson is a senior research fellow in The Heritage Foundation’s Border Security and Immigration Center and author of "The Ten Woke Commandments (You Must Not Obey)" from Academica Books.

worldStories.fullTranslation:
退役边境巡逻队队长克里斯·克莱姆（Chris Clem）探讨了一支由600多名移民组成的队伍，他们正从洪都拉斯穿过墨西哥前往美国。

早在2023年8月，数百名外国公民就曾在得克萨斯州布朗斯维尔和埃尔帕索的官方过境点发起的数起独立事件中强行冲击美国边境。国土安全部官员设立了实体路障，并切断了通往盖特韦国际大桥（Gateway International Bridge）的交通。在墨西哥一侧，军方进行了干预，以阻止外籍人员进一步大规模非法入境美国的企图。

对于那些已经遗忘的人来说，我们不久前每个月都面临着数十万不得入境的外籍人员涌入边境。为什么他们在2021至2024年间数以百万计地涌来，而今天只有区区几百人？这是政策抉择的结果。前总统乔·拜登及其国土安全部长亚历杭德罗·马约卡斯（Alejandro Mayorkas）在炮制虚构的“合法途径”以及绕过我们的法律、尽可能多地将外籍人员予以假释或释放进入我国方面，取得了令人痛心的“成功”。其影响将持续数十年。

最近，我们在位于北非的西班牙城市休达（Ceuta）看到了拜登边境政策的回响。今年7月，7.2万多名非西班牙籍人员强行冲击边境，而摩洛哥几乎未采取任何阻止措施。其中大多数是摩洛哥人，大部分人在几天内便返回了家中。但有1万人或更多来自撒哈拉以南非洲，或者声称自己是未成年人，抑或两者兼有。

数千名移民冲垮边境飞地致至少18人死亡，西班牙部署军队

西班牙如今不得不根据欧洲极其软弱的庇护政策来处理这些人，这很可能导致许多人被带往西班牙本土。哪怕这些冲击者中只有极少数人成功进入欧洲，也将鼓励更多的人去尝试。

在西班牙陆军的护送下，越境进入西班牙的移民于2026年8月1日周六从西班牙飞地休达返回摩洛哥。（美联社图片/Antonio Sempere）

唐纳德·特朗普总统终结了拜登的开放边境政策。国土安全部表示，自他上任以来，边境上“抓了就放”的案例为零。特朗普还叫停了拜登鲁莽且非法的群体假释计划。虽然仍有一些外籍人员在未被抓获的情况下潜入，但数量已大大减少，因为边境巡逻队现在有充足的时间和人力去搜寻他们，并拥有拘留他们的法定授权。

边境抓捕量骤降94%，特朗普政府创下连续15个月边境释放为零的纪录

特朗普的果断行动遏制了这场人造灾难，此前该灾难导致多达1000万非法外籍人员在毫无背景审查且几乎没有资格获得庇护的情况下进入我国。但特朗普无法改变大规模移民等式中的“需求端”。世界上仍然存在大量贫困、治理失序的国家。

诚然，也有一些成功范例。包括阿根廷、玻利维亚、智利、哥伦比亚、哥斯达黎加和秘鲁在内的整个拉美地区的选举中，保守派领导人取代了左翼领导人，这为我们半球的安全与繁荣带来了好兆头。

坦维·拉特纳（TANVI RATNA）：拉美的右倾转向正在重塑美国的后院

在萨尔瓦多，总统纳伊布·布克尔（Nayib Bukele）大幅削减了犯罪率并改善了经济，以至于该国目前极度匮乏劳动力。美国拿下委内瑞拉总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗，并换上一位更具合作精神的领导人（尽管仍属左翼），应能改善该国经济，并使数以百万计的人得以安全返乡。

但在拉美、非洲和亚洲的其他地方，恶劣的政府治理、疲软的经济和高生育率继续驱使人们想要离开。美国依然是一个广受青睐的目的地。

欧洲亦是如此，那里的本土人口正逐渐被来自“全球南方”的大规模移民所取代。这不是阴谋论，而是一个肉眼可见的人口学现象。

联合国难民署（UNHCR）估计，休达至少有1200名移民可能符合在西班牙获得庇护的条件。联合国难民署与国际移民组织（IOM）利用数百万美元的美国资金，将来自世界各地的非法移民经由拉美输送到美国。

移民危机迫使意大利恢复对西班牙的边境管控，欧洲开放边境体系遭受考验

声称申请庇护以便进入西班牙和更大的欧盟范围，正是驱使人们冲击休达的动机，就像过去冲击美国边境的人一样。他们想要工作和更好的前景，包括慷慨的福利待遇。但绝大多数人在本国并未遭受符合庇护条件的那种迫害。他们自己也承认这一点，至少在庇护程序启动、他们不得不编造一套说辞并坚持到底之前是这样。

唐纳德·特朗普总统终结了拜登的开放边境政策。国土安全部表示，自他上任以来，边境上“抓了就放”的案例为零。特朗普还叫停了拜登鲁莽且非法的群体假释计划。

一名来自乍得的休达非法移民穆罕默德·亚库卜（Mohamed Yaqoub）告诉美联社记者：“对我们来说，最重要的是拿到身份文件”，这样他就能实现去法国留学的目标。如果他真的是在寻求庇护，亚库卜本应在离开乍得后抵达的第一个安全国家提出申请。他不仅没有这样做，而且承认一旦拿到“身份”，他甚至不会留在西班牙，而是会前往法国。

边境冲击后仍有数千名移民滞留西班牙领土，死亡人数达约100人：休达官员

从全球南方迁移到富裕国家的需求是难以满足的。然而，住房、医疗和福利资源是有限的。许多欧盟成员国由于经济增长乏力，同时社会主义医疗和养老金体系成本不断上升，面临着结构性预算赤字和债务危机。

点击此处阅读更多福克斯新闻观点文章

美国在很大程度上也处于同一境地。如今，与欧洲一样，我们有证据表明，典型的非法移民或低技能合法移民在其一生中会带来净财政损失——因此不仅没有挽救社会保障制度，反而拖垮了它。

点击此处下载福克斯新闻应用程序

让休达和布朗斯维尔成为我们的警钟，绝不能让拜登时期的边境乱象重演。

西蒙·汉金森（Simon Hankinson）是传统基金会（The Heritage Foundation）边境安全与移民中心的高级研究员，著有由阿卡德米卡图书公司（Academica Books）出版的《不可服从的十大觉醒诫条》（The Ten Woke Commandments (You Must Not Obey)）。

worldStories.originalTitle: Jon Rahm to quit LIV Golf tour over ‘unacceptable’ terms
worldStories.source: Al Jazeera (半岛电视台官方英文)
worldStories.snippet: 'Rahm has reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and has determined that they are unacceptable,' his lawyer said.
worldStories.fullContent:
‘Rahm has reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and has determined that they are unacceptable,’ his lawyer said.

Former world number one Jon Rahm has said he is quitting LIV Golf, robbing ⁠the breakaway circuit of ⁠one of its biggest stars while it fights to emerge from bankruptcy.

Rahm’s lawyer John Beck told a bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday that the two-time ⁠major champion made his decision after looking over details of LIV Golf’s planned next phase.

“Mr Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0, as the parties have been referring to ⁠it, and has determined that those terms are unacceptable as to him, and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0,” Beck told the court.

Other golfers asked a US bankruptcy judge to help terminate their contracts and clarify their ability to negotiate with other tournament organisers and sponsors ‌as their LIV contracts go unpaid.

LIV has already agreed to terminate Sergio Garcia’s contract after determining that the league would not honour its terms, and lawyers for Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith, An Byeong-hun, Marc Leishman, Cameron Tringale and Matthew Wolff asked the judge to allow those players out of their old contracts.

Ending those contracts would not preclude those players from agreeing to participate in LIV 2.0.

Rahm, one of the most high-profile players to join LIV Golf, has won three consecutive season-long individual titles on LIV since joining the circuit ⁠in late 2023, eight months after winning the Masters for his second major title.

When LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 protection in New ⁠Jersey last month, its filing listed several star golfers as ⁠creditors still owed millions in unsecured claims. Among them, Rahm had the largest claim among players at $7.5m.

Earlier this week, LIV secured funding from BC Partners to help it emerge from restructuring and strengthen its financial footing before the 2027 ‌season. The financing, up to $300m, remains subject to bankruptcy court approval and customary conditions.

BC Partners Credit, which provides financing to middle-market companies, said the funding would support what it described ‌as ‌the next phase of LIV Golf, under which players would become equity owners of the league and its teams.

其律师表示：“拉姆审阅了拟议中的‘LIV 2.0’条款，并判定这些条款令人无法接受。”

前世界第一琼·拉姆（Jon Rahm）表示他将退出LIV高尔夫（LIV Golf）。在该分离派巡回赛正竭力摆脱破产困境之际，此举使其痛失旗下的最大牌明星之一。

拉姆的律师约翰·贝克（John Beck）在周三的破产听证会上表示，这位两届大满贯冠军得主是在查阅了LIV高尔夫规划中下一阶段的细节后做出这一决定的。

贝克对法庭表示：“拉姆先生已独立审查了各方所称的‘LIV 2.0’拟议条款，并认定这些条款对他而言是无法接受的，他今后将不会参与‘LIV 2.0’。”

鉴于LIV合同款项未获支付，其他高尔夫球手也请求美国破产法官协助解除他们的合同，并明确他们与其他赛事组织者及赞助商进行谈判的权利。

在认定联盟将无法履行其条款后，LIV已同意解除塞尔吉奥·加西亚（Sergio Garcia）的合同，而布赖森·德尚博（Bryson DeChambeau）、卡梅隆·史密斯（Cameron Smith）、安秉勋（An Byeong-hun）、马克·利什曼（Marc Leishman）、卡梅隆·特林加尔（Cameron Tringale）和马修·沃尔夫（Matthew Wolff）的律师也请求法官允许这些球员摆脱旧合同。

终止旧合同并不会阻止这些球员后续同意参与“LIV 2.0”。

拉姆是加盟LIV高尔夫的最瞩目球员之一。他在2023年底加入该巡回赛（此前八个月他刚赢得美国大师赛，夺得个人第二座大满贯冠军），自加盟以来已在LIV连续斩获三个赛季的个人总冠军。

上个月LIV高尔夫在新泽西州申请第11章破产保护时，其申报文件将数名明星球手列为债权人，仍拖欠数百万美元的无担保债权。其中，拉姆在球员中的债权金额最高，达到750万美元。

本周早些时候，LIV获得了来自BC Partners的资金支持，以帮助其摆脱重组并在2027赛季前巩固财务基础。这笔高达3亿美元的融资仍需破产法院批准并满足惯常条件。

为中型市场公司提供融资的BC Partners Credit表示，这笔资金将支持其所谓的LIV高尔夫下一阶段，届时球员将成为该联盟及其下属车队/战队的股权持有人。

worldStories.title: 休·休伊特：中期选举仅剩一个月——你需要了解其中的利害关系
worldStories.originalTitle: HUGH HEWITT: The midterms are one month out — you need to know the stakes
worldStories.snippet: Chuck Schumer would block federal judges and Supreme Court nominees if Democrats win the Senate, using McConnell's own precedent against him.
worldStories.fullContent:
Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., discusses Senate Democrats blocking key bills, including the Ratepayer Protection Act. McCormick also analyzes economic policy, socialism and the conflict with Iran.

The short answer: If a "blue wave" materializes, the nation’s national security will be greatly compromised and almost no new federal judges or cabinet appointments of any kind will occur. The sort of defense spending the country definitely and urgently needs will not be appropriated, and if he becomes majority leader in the Senate, Chuck Schumer will shut down confirmations of almost all nominees from President Trump.

What difference would those changes make?

On the one hand — the hand that keeps a history textbook open — the answer is "not much." People expecting a "blue wave" may be disappointed that one or both of the houses of Congress don’t flip on election night, but even if they do, a different kind of disappointment awaits the Left

LEE CARTER: POLLS SAY DEMOCRATS COULD SWAMP REPUBLICANS. AS A POLLSTER, I HAVE A QUESTION

First, even the rosiest of scenarios for the left doesn’t give Democrats veto-proof majorities in both legislative chambers, the sort of one-party governance that, for example, that has wrecked California. Divided government is a recipe for repeating government shutdowns which can annoy and even destroy some things, but cannot bring about fundamental change.

Democrats in D.C. cannot make all of America into California or New York without at least partisan control of all three branches of government and even then the sort of change the Democratic Socialists of America demand — abolition of the Senate and packing the Supreme Court are two of their "must haves" — require at least super majorities and probably Constitutional amendments.

SOCIALISTS LAUNCH RADICAL PLATFORM TO ABOLISH THE US SENATE IN BID TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM AMERICA

The fever dreams of the Left are thus going to remain unfulfilled for a very long time, because, no matter how often the "No Kings" canasta parties gather, the Constitution is very strong and doesn’t yield to fits of high revolutionary passion. It was built with the danger of precipitous legislative action in mind and, because deliberation is a feature, not a bug, of our constitutional order, it is rare indeed when anything happens fast.

But significant damage would be done nonetheless, especially to national security spending. A lame duck Congress run by Republicans could try and pass a three-year defense appropriation, but if it can’t get that done between November 4, 2026, and January 3, 2027, the American military will be subject again to the sort of national security self-harm done during the years of "the Sequester."

Democratic control of the Senate is also almost a guarantee that not a single federal appeals court or Supreme Court nominee would pass through a Chuck Schumer-managed Senate. Schumer would simply roll tape of then-Senate Majority Leader McConnell announcing "no hearings, no votes" in the aftermath of the untimely death of Justice Scalia. Schumer will argue that McConnell set the precedent.

The optics of the different situations between McConnell’s refusal to move Merrick Garland forward in 2020 and those that result if a narrow Democratic Senate majority in 2027 blocks a vote on a Supreme Court nominee might be dramatic enough to wear down Democrats' resolve for revenge, but probably even a terrible look would not budge such a boycott and certainly not in 2028. Schumer would also likely refuse to allow votes on non-judicial Trump nominees no matter how far out the next election. His hold on the job of leader would be gone the instant he permitted a floor vote on any nominee of consequence, unless he was certain of the votes to defeat that nominee.

MAJORITY LEADER THUNE WARNS CHUCK SCHUMER 'LIVES IN FEAR' OF SOCIALISTS TAKING OVER DEMOCRATIC PARTY

We also know that the hard-left of the Democratic Senate nominees this year — Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, James Talarico in Texas, Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Chris Pappas in New Hampshire and Mary Peltola in Alaska — will be united with the anti-defense doves already in the Democratic caucus. What the country must have — a budgeted demand signal for the defense-industrial base — will flicker out. The rebirth of American shipbuilding will disappear too, even as China’s Communist Party cheers on the smothering blanket of big government regulation of AI/SI descending on its competitors in the United States.

So a "blue wave" would do great damage, but there are some things such a wave could not do.

President Trump’s continued command of the American military would be unimpaired, for example, nor would such a wave wipe out the re-mooring to the Constitution that has been ongoing at the Supreme Court for the past decade.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

So a blue wave would be very bad news, but it wouldn’t overturn the Republic. GOP candidates are on firm ground with warnings about the mess that would follow giving majorities to Democrats but should avoid hysteria. Our adversaries abroad who are hoping for a Democratic wave should also remember that President George W. Bush ordered "the surge" after Republicans got "thumped" in 2006. If the rump regime in Iran is counting on Democrats to save it from Trump, they could not be more wrong.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Vote Republican to keep the country defended and the Constitution intact. But don’t do so because the Republic is in peril. It’s not. Yet.

Hugh Hewitt is a Fox News contributor and host of "The Hugh Hewitt Show" heard weekday afternoons from 3 PM to 6 PM ET on the Salem Radio Network, and simulcast on Salem News Channel. Hugh drives Americans home on the East Coast and to lunch on the West Coast on over 400 affiliates nationwide, and on all the streaming platforms where SNC can be seen. He is a frequent guest on the Fox News Channel’s news roundtable, hosted by Bret Baier weekdays at 6pm ET. A son of Ohio and a graduate of Harvard College and the University of Michigan Law School, Hewitt has been a Professor of Law at Chapman University’s Fowler School of Law since 1996 where he teaches Constitutional Law. Hewitt launched his eponymous radio show from Los Angeles in 1990. Hewitt has frequently appeared on every major national news television network, hosted television shows for PBS and MSNBC, written for every major American paper, has authored a dozen books and moderated a score of Republican candidate debates, most recently the November 2023 Republican presidential debate in Miami and four Republican presidential debates in the 2015-16 cycle. Hewitt focuses his radio show and his column on the Constitution, national security, American politics and the Cleveland Browns and Guardians. Hewitt has interviewed tens of thousands of guests from Democrats Hillary Clinton and John Kerry to Republican Presidents George W. Bush and Donald Trump over his 40 years in broadcasting. This column previews the lead story that will drive his radio/ TV show today.
