aiStories.title: 印度驳斥埃隆·马斯克关于星链落地遭遇歧视的指控
aiStories.originalTitle: India rejects Elon Musk’s claim of discrimination over Starlink launch
aiStories.snippet: Starlink is still awaiting security clearance before it can seek spectrum and begin commercial services in India.
aiStories.fullContent:
India has rejected Elon Musk’s claim that Starlink, SpaceX’s satellite internet service, is being unfairly blocked from launching in the country. The pushback comes as SpaceX struggles to turn years of regulatory work and partnerships with India’s biggest telecom operators into a commercial launch in one of the world’s largest internet markets.

On Wednesday, Musk accused unnamed “oligarchs” of blocking Starlink’s launch in India to maintain what he called their “monopolistic chokehold” on the country, without identifying them or providing evidence for his claim. He called the alleged blocking a “crime against the people of India” and argued that Starlink could bring affordable, high-speed internet to people who lack internet access.

Hours later, India’s Ministry of Communications pushed back, saying its regulatory framework for satellite communications is “fair and non-discriminatory.” The ministry said in a statement that Starlink and two other licensed satellite operators are all at “broadly the same regulatory stage.” It added that all three companies are undergoing security assessments that must be completed before they can seek spectrum, the radio frequencies that satellites use to send signal.

Musk’s comments came hours after Lauren Dreyer, Starlink’s vice president of business operations, appeared at a telecom industry conference, India Mobile Congress, in New Delhi and reiterated the company’s commitment to the market. “We stand ready to serve India,” Dreyer said, adding that Starlink wants to help realize Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s goal of achieving universal connectivity across the country.

Starlink said it already has more than 20 gateway sites (the ground stations that link its satellites to the internet) and hundreds of antennas on the ground in India, and has adapted its operations to meet the country’s regulatory, security, and data-sovereignty requirements. Moreover, SpaceX has positioned its satellite network as a complement to — rather than a replacement for — India’s terrestrial telecom networks.

SpaceX first attempted to launch Starlink in India in 2021. The company, however, had to refund preorders for its equipment in early 2022 after the Indian government called it out for “booking/rendering the satellite internet service” before getting the necessary licenses.

Starlink has also previously clashed with India’s largest telecom operators over how satellite spectrum should be allocated. Starlink pushed for spectrum to be assigned administratively, while Reliance Jio argued that it should be auctioned — a position that could have made Starlink’s entry more expensive. India ultimately sided with Starlink’s preferred approach, deciding to allocate satellite spectrum administratively rather than through an auction.

Jio and Airtel, the two biggest Indian telcos, are also pursuing their own satellite internet services, even as they have agreed to distribute Starlink in India. Jio is working with satellite operator SES on satellite broadband, while Airtel is a major backer of Eutelsat OneWeb, another licensed satellite operator in India.

While the timing of Starlink’s India launch remains unclear, the company this week launched Starlink Mobile, which connects ordinary phones to satellites, in neighboring Bangladesh this week.

Starlink, India’s Ministry of Communications, Reliance Jio, and Bharti Airtel did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
印度驳斥了埃隆·马斯克的说法，马斯克此前称其旗下的太空探索技术公司（SpaceX）卫星互联网服务“星链”（Starlink）在该国开展业务遭到了不公正的阻碍。SpaceX多年来一直致力于在监管合规以及与印度最大电信运营商建立合作方面推进落地，以期在全球最大的互联网市场之一实现商业化运营，而印度的反驳正是在这一关键时刻做出的。

周三，马斯克指责未具名的“寡头”阻挠星链在印度的落地，目的是维持其所谓的对该国的“垄断扼杀”，但他并未点出具体对象，也未就其指控提供证据。他称所谓的阻挠行为是“对印度人民的犯罪”，并坚称星链可以为那些缺乏网络连接的人口提供负担得起的高速互联网服务。

数小时后，印度通信部做出反驳，称其卫星通信监管框架是“公平且无歧视的”。该部在一份声明中表示，星链与另外两家获得许可的卫星运营商都处于“大体相同的监管阶段”。声明还补充道，这三家公司目前都在接受安全评估，在申请卫星传输信号所用的无线电频率（频谱）之前，必须先完成该评估。

马斯克发表上述言论的数小时前，星链业务运营副总裁劳伦·德雷尔（Lauren Dreyer）刚刚出席了在新德里举行的印度移动大会（India Mobile Congress）电信行业峰会，并重申了公司对该市场的承诺。德雷尔表示：“我们随时准备好为印度提供服务。”她还补充说，星链希望助力实现印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪在全国普及网络连接的目标。

星链表示，它已在印度拥有20多个网关站点（将卫星连接到互联网的地面站）和数百个地面天线，并调整了业务运营，以满足该国在监管、安全以及数据主权方面的要求。此外，SpaceX将自己的卫星网络定位为对印度地面电信网络的补充，而非替代品。

SpaceX最初于2021年尝试在印度推出星链服务。然而，在印度政府指出其在获得必要牌照之前便“接受预订/提供卫星互联网服务”后，该公司不得不在2022年初退还了设备的预订款项。

此前，星链还曾就卫星频谱的分配方式与印度最大的电信运营商发生过冲突。星链主张通过行政方式分配频谱，而信实工业旗下的Jio则认为应当采取竞拍方式——若采取竞拍可能会使星链的准入门槛成本大幅上升。印度最终采纳了星链所偏向的方案，决定以行政方式而非竞拍方式分配卫星频谱。

印度最大的两家电信运营商Jio和Airtel虽然已同意在印度代销星链服务，但也都在推进各自的卫星互联网业务。Jio正与卫星运营商SES合作开展卫星宽带业务，而Airtel则是印度另一家持牌卫星运营商Eutelsat OneWeb的主要支持者。

尽管星链在印度的上线时间仍不明确，但该公司本周在邻国孟加拉国推出了“星链移动”（Starlink Mobile）服务，可将普通智能手机直接与卫星相连。

星链、印度通信部、Reliance Jio以及Bharti Airtel未立即回应置评请求。

aiStories.title: 机器人数据初创公司 Mecka AI 获红杉资本领投的 6000 万美元融资
aiStories.originalTitle: Robot data startup Mecka AI nabs $60M from Sequoia
aiStories.snippet: Mecka AI collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots. The startup pays people to record everyday tasks.
aiStories.fullContent:
Mecka AI, a startup that collects and analyzes human motion data to train humanoid robots and other kinds of robots, announced it has raised a $60 million Series B round led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Microsoft’s venture fund M12, and others. TechCrunch had previously reported that the startup was nearing a new funding round at a $500 million valuation.

Founded in 2024, the startup intends to do for robotics what Scale AI, Mercor, Surge, and other data-labeling companies have done for LLMs. Those companies supply the human-generated data these systems learn from. Mecka pays people to record themselves doing everyday tasks, like making coffee or fixing cars, while wearing body sensors and using smartphones.

Other startups that collect real-world data for robot training include XDOF, which was in talks to raise a Series B round at a $1.2 billion valuation according to TechCrunch’s previous reporting. Human-data platforms that began with LLMs are also expanding into robotics, such as Scale AI and Micro1.

aiStories.title: 当风投涌入旧金山之际，Endeavor Catalyst为“他处”的创始人筹集3.2亿美元
aiStories.originalTitle: While VCs crowd into San Francisco, Endeavor Catalyst raises $320M for founders ‘elsewhere’
aiStories.snippet: Endeavor Catalyst just raised $320 million to keep backing founders outside Silicon Valley. Half the profits go back to the nonprofit that finds them.
aiStories.fullContent:
Endeavor Catalyst has closed its fifth fund with $320 million in capital commitments, bringing the firm’s total assets under management to more than $850 million. The raise is good news for founders outside the Bay Area who risk getting overlooked as more funds focus squarely on AI companies in Silicon Valley.

Endeavor Catalyst is the venture arm of Endeavor, a New York-based global nonprofit that has spent 30 years supporting founders outside major tech hubs. (It calls all those other places “elsewhere” throughout its marketing materials.)

The fund is run by managing partner Allen Taylor, a 20-year veteran of the organization, and managing director Jackie Carmel, who joined Endeavor Catalyst 12 years ago, along with a 16-person team. The official general partner, though, is Endeavor itself. What that means, says Linda Rottenberg, who co-founded Endeavor and helped start Endeavor Catalyst in 2012, is that “half of the fund’s profits go back to Endeavor, so every investment helps the next generation of founders who are building elsewhere.”

The bar for those founders is pretty high. A person first has to get into Endeavor’s network, where he or she can access Endeavor’s mentoring and extensive network, and that’s hard. Last year, the group says it screened more than 10,000 candidates and picked 88. The network now has more than 3,100 entrepreneurs in over 50 countries.

When one of those founders’ companies raises at least $5 million in a round led by another institutional investor, Endeavor Catalyst can join in on the same terms as that lead. The team tells TechCrunch that checks usually run $1 million to $3 million but can’t exceed 10% of the round.

Over the next few years, they plan to make 40 to 50 investments annually, investing in up to 150 companies altogether with this new fund, they say.

Taylor, via an email exchange, wouldn’t share numbers on cash-on-cash returns tied to its earlier funds, but he did point to some impressive-sounding numbers. Across all five funds, he says, Endeavor Catalyst has backed 437 companies in 44 markets. Eighty-three of those startups are currently valued at $1 billion or more, he says, and the unit has seen 39 exits and 11 IPOs.

Some of the venture arm’s most valuable holdings right now include four-year-old ElevenLabs, the maker of AI voice tools that was recently valued at $22 billion in a secondary sale (it was founded in Poland originally), and Bending Spoons, the 13-year-old Italy-based conglomerate that went public in July and that currently boasts a $26 billion market cap.

Other holdings include New York-based Reflection AI (founded by two former Google DeepMind researchers — one of whom was born in Greece), which is now valued at $25 billion; Checkout.com, whose founder is Swiss and which was valued last year at $12 billion; the African payments infrastructure company Flutterwave, valued this summer at $3.2 billion; and AI coding startup Replit, co-founded by Amjad Masad, who is Palestinian-Jordanian. Replit snagged a $9 billion valuation earlier this year.

Endeavor, the nonprofit, has especially well-connected people associated with it, including board members Reid Hoffman; Nick Beim, a career VC who has spent the last 25 years at Matrix Partners, then Venrock; and Edgar Bronfman Jr., the former head of Warner Music and Seagram, who chairs Endeavor’s board.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is a longtime friend of Endeavor, too, having gone to Harvard with Rottenberg. (Late last month in San Francisco, I sat down with him during a rare visit to the Bay Area that was organized by Endeavor and where he met with tech founders and Greek expatriates.)

Altogether, Endeavor Catalyst’s newest fund includes 400 limited partners, including Hoffman; famed hedge fund manager Bill Ackman; and the Dutch investment group Prosus. According to Taylor, roughly 30% of those backers are Endeavor founders themselves, including founders of Nubank, Revolut, and Checkout.com.

While so much attention is paid to what’s happening in San Francisco and its immediate environs right now, the bets of Endeavor Catalyst suggest what other investors may be missing, and Endeavor, with local teams and mentors in dozens of countries, seems particularly well-positioned to see it.

Indeed, about 90% of the venture arm’s investments are outside the U.S., it says. Europe is its fastest-growing region, with 12 new investments in the first half of 2026 compared with 14 in all of last year, though Latin America is still the largest.

Repeat founders are also becoming a bigger part of the mix. Taylor tells TechCrunch that roughly 14% of Endeavor Catalyst’s fourth fund went to second companies started by Endeavor founders at the seed or Series A stage. With this new fund, the team expects that number will reach 20%.

Pictured above: Endeavor co-founder Linda Rottenberg onstage in Turin, Italy, earlier this month.

Endeavor Catalyst已完成第五支基金的募集，获得3.2亿美元资本承诺，使该机构管理的资产总额超过8.5亿美元。对于湾区以外的创始人来说，这一募资消息令人振奋；随着越来越多的基金将重点明确放在硅谷的人工智能公司上，他们面临着被忽视的风险。

Endeavor Catalyst是总部位于纽约的全球性非营利组织Endeavor旗下的风险投资部门。30年来，Endeavor一直支持主要科技中心以外的创始人。（在其营销材料中，Endeavor把所有这些其他地方统称为“他处”。）

该基金由管理合伙人艾伦·泰勒和董事总经理杰基·卡梅尔，以及一个由16人组成的团队负责运营。泰勒在该组织任职已有20年，卡梅尔则于12年前加入Endeavor Catalyst。不过，名义上的普通合伙人是Endeavor本身。Endeavor联合创始人、并于2012年协助创办Endeavor Catalyst的琳达·罗滕伯格表示，这意味着“基金利润的一半会回流Endeavor，因此每一笔投资都在帮助下一代在他处创业的创始人”。

这些创始人的门槛相当高。一个人首先必须进入Endeavor的网络，在那里可以获得Endeavor的指导以及广泛的人脉，而这并不容易。该组织称，去年他们筛选了超过1万名候选人，最终选中了88人。目前，这一网络已覆盖50多个国家的逾3100名企业家。

当其中一位创始人的公司完成一轮至少500万美元、且由另一家机构投资者领投的融资时，Endeavor Catalyst可以按照与领投方相同的条款参与投资。该团队告诉TechCrunch，其支票金额通常为100万至300万美元，但不得超过该轮融资总额的10%。

他们表示，未来几年计划每年进行40至50笔投资，并利用这支新基金总共投资最多150家公司。

泰勒在电子邮件交流中不愿透露与此前几支基金相关的现金回报倍数，但他提到了一些听起来颇为亮眼的数字。他说，综合五支基金，Endeavor Catalyst已支持44个市场的437家公司。其中83家初创公司目前估值达到或超过10亿美元，该部门已实现39次退出和11次首次公开募股（IPO）。

目前，该风险投资部门最有价值的部分持股包括成立四年的ElevenLabs。这家公司开发人工智能语音工具，最近在一笔二级交易中的估值达到220亿美元（该公司最初创立于波兰）；此外还有总部位于意大利、成立已有13年的综合企业Bending Spoons。后者于今年7月上市，目前市值达到260亿美元。

其他持股还包括总部位于纽约的Reflection AI。该公司由两名前Google DeepMind研究人员共同创办，其中一人出生于希腊，目前估值为250亿美元；Checkout.com，其创始人为瑞士人，去年估值为120亿美元；非洲支付基础设施公司Flutterwave，今年夏季估值为32亿美元；以及人工智能编程初创公司Replit，该公司由巴勒斯坦裔约旦人阿姆贾德·马萨德共同创办。Replit今年早些时候获得了90亿美元估值。

这家非营利组织Endeavor的关联人士人脉极为广泛，其中包括董事会成员里德·霍夫曼；职业风险投资人尼克·拜姆，他过去25年先后任职于Matrix Partners和Venrock；以及华纳音乐和Seagram前负责人埃德加·布朗夫曼 Jr.，后者担任Endeavor董事会主席。

希腊总理基里亚科斯·米佐塔基斯也是Endeavor的长期好友，他与罗滕伯格曾一同就读于哈佛大学。（上月底，我在旧金山与他进行了会面。当时他罕见地访问湾区，此行由Endeavor组织，他还与科技创始人和希腊侨民进行了交流。）

Endeavor Catalyst的新基金总计拥有400家有限合伙人，其中包括霍夫曼、著名对冲基金经理比尔·阿克曼以及荷兰投资集团Prosus。泰勒称，约30%的出资者本身就是Endeavor的创始人，其中包括Nubank、Revolut和Checkout.com的创始人。

当前，人们将大量注意力放在旧金山及其周边地区发生的事情上，而Endeavor Catalyst的投资选择表明，其他投资者可能忽视了一些机会。Endeavor在数十个国家设有当地团队和导师，因此似乎尤其有能力发现这些机会。

Endeavor Catalyst表示，其风险投资部门约90%的投资都在美国以外。欧洲是其增长最快的地区，2026年上半年新增12笔投资，而去年全年为14笔，不过拉丁美洲仍然是最大的市场。

连续创业者在其投资组合中所占的比重也在上升。泰勒告诉TechCrunch，Endeavor Catalyst第四支基金约14%的资金投向了由Endeavor创始人创办的第二家公司，投资阶段为种子轮或A轮。对于这支新基金，该团队预计这一比例将达到20%。

上图：本月早些时候，Endeavor联合创始人琳达·罗滕伯格在意大利都灵登台演讲。

Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All Transportation

The iX4 is a sportier spin on the iX3, with the same powerful Gen6 battery providing class-leading range.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Andrew J. Hawkins

While much of the automotive world sits dumbfounded as China gobbles up all its customers, BMW continues to roll out extremely well-crafted, technologically advanced electric vehicles that impress in both drive quality and price. The latest is the BMW iX4, a coupe-shaped SUV that puts a sportier spin on the automaker’s iX3.

The iX4 is the third vehicle to be released on BMW’s next-generation Neue Klasse platform, following the iX3 and i3 models. The iX4 50 xDrive will come first in March 2027, followed by an even more high-performance M60 xDrive version later in the year. The automaker is positioning this new lineup as its bulwark against the flood of Chinese imports that is currently decimating other European brands. But while the iX4 can certainly compete on range and tech, it’s unclear whether BMW can rival China in terms of sheer affordability.

In that respect, the BMW iX4 50 xDrive starts at $66,200 (excluding fees for destination and handling). And it bears all the hallmarks of BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, such as the “Gen6” high-voltage battery with 112.2kWh of usable energy, an 800-volt architecture for lightning-quick charging top-ups, and up to 428 miles of range based on EPA estimates.

That’s more range than the Tesla Model Y, the best-selling electric vehicle in the world. BMW has been blowing away expectations on range to such a degree that even the experts at InsideEVs are left wondering whether it’s overkill. After all, Tesla and others have done plenty well with EVs in the mid-300s, while Lucid continues to struggle despite exceeding 500 miles in range.

But BMW wants to go the distance, believing that range and efficiency are two of its biggest selling points. The third would be performance, and thanks to a dual-motor setup in both the 50 xDrive and M60 xDrive, the iX4 is sure to delivery plenty of giddy up. The 50 xDrive’s motors put out 463 horsepower and 475lb-ft of torque, for a 0–60mph acceleration of 4.7 seconds. Meanwhile, the M60 xDrive’s motors produce 603hp and 645lb-ft of torque, for a 0–60 time a whole second less than the 50 xDrive.

Like other Neue Klasse vehicles, the electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM) in the rear axle serves as the primary drive axle, using electricity instead of permanent magnets to power both its stator outer frame and interior spinning rotor. An inverter acts as the brain of the system, converting direct current from the battery into alternating current for the motor, regulating the electromagnets, and monitoring performance to keep the motor running as efficiently as possible. BMW says this combination helps slash drive-system energy losses by 40 percent and weight by 10 percent.

The Gen6 batteries are built with cylindrical lithium-ion cells measuring 46mm in diameter and 95mm in height that provide a 20 percent increase in energy density compared to the prismatic cells used in BMW’s Gen5 batteries. BMW has eliminated the traditional modules in favor of a “pack-to-open-body” construction where the battery housing serves as the vehicle’s underbody, lowering weight and increasing torsional rigidity.

Like Hyundai and Kia, BMW is building its Neue Klasse EVs to take fast charging to the next level. With its 800V architecture, the iX4 can accept up to 400kWs of DC fast charging, replenishing up to 184 miles of range in 10 minutes, and 10–80 percent charge in just 21 minutes. With a NACS charging port, the iX4 will be compatible with over 80,000 Tesla Supercharger connectors around the world.

And like the i3 and iX3, the iX4 can do all sorts of extra stuff, including bidirectional charging with vehicle-to-load and vehicle-to-home capabilities, an intelligent charging flap that opens when a driver approaches a known charging point, and Plug & Charge for automatic charging at 10 different charging providers.

If you look at the whole package, there’s a lot to like. Sure, the Model Y beats the iX4 in a few categories, most importantly price. It’s a bit quicker off the line, and of course, the Model Y comes with the option for Full Self-Driving (Supervised). BMW has something it calls “Symbiotic Drive,” which it describes as a Level 2 system designed for “fluid, intuitive interaction.” In other words, drivers can adjust the steering or even brake without canceling the automated functions. The iX4 also allows for hands-free driving on the highway — but no point-to-point assisted driving. Not until 2027 at the earliest.

Where BMW still bests Tesla is variety. You can get the iX4 50 xDrive, or if you want something sportier, try the M60 xDrive. If you’re rather have a sedan, there’s the i3. Or if you want something a bit more affordable, there’s the iX3. And don’t forget the flagship 7 series. Yep, those are getting Neue Klasse makeovers as well.

Tesla has the Model 3 and Model Y — and that’s about it. (Yes, there’s the Cybertruck, but clearly most people aren’t interested in that. And there’s the Cybercab, but it won’t be on sale anytime soon.) BMW knows its customers want options. And it’s doing it’s best to deliver.

正当大半个汽车界眼睁睁看着中国车企蚕食其所有客户而目瞪口呆之际，宝马却在持续推出工艺精湛、技术先进的电动车型，在驾控品质和售价上均令人印象深刻。最新登场的是宝马iX4，这是一款轿跑风格的SUV，为该车企的iX3赋予了更为动感的特质。
iX4是宝马继iX3和i3之后，基于下一代“新世代”（Neue Klasse）平台推出的第三款车型。iX4 50 xDrive将于2027年3月率先上市，随后在同年晚些时候推出性能更高的M60 xDrive版本。这家汽车制造商正将这一新产品线定位为抵御中国进口车洪流的壁垒，目前这些进口车正在重创其他欧洲品牌。不过，尽管iX4在续航里程和科技配置上绝对具备竞争力，但宝马在纯粹的价格亲民度方面能否抗衡中国品牌仍属未知。
就此而言，宝马iX4 50 xDrive的起售价为66,200美元（不含目的地和装卸运输费）。它具备宝马其他“新世代”车型的所有鲜明特征，例如可用电量达112.2千瓦时的“第六代”高压电池、用于极速补能的800伏架构，以及根据EPA标准估算高达428英里（约689公里）的续航里程。
这一续航表现超越了全球最畅销电动车特斯拉Model Y。宝马在续航方面的突破已远超预期，以至于InsideEVs的专家们都在琢磨这是否属于性能过剩。毕竟，特斯拉等车企凭借300多英里续航的电动车就取得了优异成绩，而Lucid即便续航突破500英里也依然步履维艰。
但宝马希望走得更远，坚信续航和能效是其最大的两大卖点。第三大卖点则是性能，得益于50 xDrive和M60 xDrive均采用的双电机布局，iX4必将带来充沛的冲劲。50 xDrive的双电机输出功率为463马力，扭矩为475磅-英尺，0至60英里/小时加速时间为4.7秒。与此同时，M60 xDrive的电机输出功率达603马力，扭矩为645磅-英尺，0至60英里/小时加速时间比50 xDrive整整缩短了一秒。
与其他“新世代”平台车型一样，后桥上的励磁同步电机（EESM）作为主驱动轴，其定子外壳和内部旋转转子均依靠电力而非永磁体驱动。逆变器作为系统的大脑，将电池输出的直流电转换为电动机所需的交流电，调节电磁铁，并监控运行性能以确保电机尽可能高效运转。宝马表示，这一组合有助于将驱动系统的能量损耗降低40%，并将重量减轻10%。
第六代电池采用直径46毫米、高95毫米的圆柱形锂离子电芯，与宝马第五代电池所用的方形电芯相比，能量密度提升了20%。宝马取消了传统的模组，转而采用“电池包与开放式车身一体化”（pack-to-open-body）结构，由电池外壳兼作车辆底盘，从而降低了车重并提高了扭转刚度。
与现代和起亚一样，宝马打造的“新世代”电动车旨在将快速充电推向新高度。凭借其800V高压架构，iX4可承受高达400千瓦的直流快充，10分钟内即可补充高达184英里的续航里程，10%充至80%仅需21分钟。凭借NACS充电接口，iX4将能兼容全球超过8万个特斯拉超级充电桩接口。
并且与i3和iX3一样，iX4还能提供多种额外功能，包括具备对外放电（V2L）和车对家庭供电（V2H）能力的双向充电、当驾驶员靠近已知充电桩时自动开启的智能充电盖板，以及可在10家不同充电服务运营商处实现自动充电的即插即充（Plug & Charge）功能。
纵观全局，该车亮点颇多。诚然，Model Y在某些方面依然胜过iX4，最核心的便是价格。Model Y的起步加速稍快一些，而且当然也提供了全自动驾驶（有监督）系统的选装配置。宝马则推出了名为“共生驾驶”（Symbiotic Drive）的系统，将其描述为专为“流畅、直观的交互”而设计的L2级辅助驾驶系统。换言之，驾驶员可以在不解除自动驾驶功能的情况下微调方向盘甚至刹车。iX4还支持高速公路脱手驾驶——但不支持点到点辅助驾驶，这项功能最早也要到2027年才会推出。
宝马依然领先于特斯拉的地方在于产品多样性。你可以选择iX4 50 xDrive，如果想要更具运动感的体验，可以尝试M60 xDrive。如果你更倾向于轿车，还有i3可选。或者如果你想要价格更亲民的选择，还有iX3。别忘了旗舰7系，是的，它们也将迎来“新世代”平台的革新升级。
特斯拉旗下只有Model 3和Model Y——基本仅此而已。（没错，虽然有Cybertruck，但显然大多数人对它并不感冒；还有Cybercab，但它短时间内根本不会上市销售。）宝马深知其客户渴望多样化的选择，并且正在竭尽全力予以满足。

The end could be nigh for the iconic OP-1 according to a Highsnobiety interview.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Terrence O'Brien

Teenage Engineering founder and CEO Jesper Kouthoofd told Highsnobiety that it plans to stop making synths. And yes, that includes the iconic OP-1, which put the company on the map. TE isn’t just a music gear maker; it’s also a sought-after design firm. It’s collaborated with Ikea, Nothing, and Playdate, among others. But almost everything the company makes itself — the OP-1, the OP-XY, EP-133, TP-7, et cetera — is music or audio-focused. Which makes the supposed decision to abandon the market all the more confusing.

Here’s the relevant quote from Highsnobiety:

Kouthoofd tells me that, as part of a reorganization last fall, he announced to his team he is planning to stop making synthesizers altogether. The OP-1 is no exception. Launched in 2011, it put Teenage Engineering on the map and has been central to its success ever since.

“Everyone was like, ‘What are you talking about?’ But I’ve come to the conclusion that, for us, the products aren’t the business,” Kouthoofd says. “We can be so much more than that.”

Teenage Engineering did not immediately return a request for comment.

aiStories.originalTitle: Nous Research confirms it hit $1.5B valuation, launches AI agents for business users
aiStories.snippet: The developer of Hermes Agent raised a $90 million Series B.
aiStories.fullContent:
Nous Research, the startup developing the open source Hermes Agent, has raised a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation, confirming TechCrunch’s earlier reporting.

The round was led by Robot Ventures, with participation from other backers including Nvidia, Union Square Ventures, Menlo Ventures, Samsung, and 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner. The new financing brings the three-year-old startup’s total funding to $158 million.

Popular among developers and individuals, the open source Hermes Agent has been cloned more than 24 million times, driving roughly 2.5% of global AI token usage, according to the startup’s estimates.

The capital will fund Nous Research’s push into the enterprise sector with “Hermes for Businesses,” allowing companies to deploy customized AI agents that can handle multi-step workflows while keeping their data private and secure.

Nous was at roughly $36 million in annualized revenue by mid-September 2026 and expects to pass $100 million before the end of 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Di Benedetto / The Verge A common misconception I've seen with Googlebooks is that the Quick Insert and Google logo keys are new. They're not, as they first debuted a couple of years ago on some Chromebooks. But there is something new for Googlebooks that's ripped straight from Android phones circa 2014. aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

An oldie but a goodie — and kind of a necessity-die.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Antonio G. Di Benedetto

A common misconception I’ve seen with Googlebooks is that the Quick Insert and Google logo keys are new. They’re not, as they first debuted a couple of years ago on some Chromebooks. But there is something new for Googlebooks that’s ripped straight from Android phones circa 2014.

It’s useful to have these buttons, and to have them matched across all Googlebooks. The back button seems sometimes necessary when using Android apps that aren’t really optimized for a desktop interface or mouse controls. I just wish a second press of the home button brought all your apps back to where they were, but that’s another feature called desktop peeking that uses a different keyboard shortcut.

If you’re an Android nerd of yore, it’s kind of fun to see these buttons live on. But they’re also a reminder that you sometimes need a fallback when Android gets all Android on you.

我经常看到关于 Googlebook 的一个普遍误解，就是认为“快速插入”（Quick Insert）键和 Google 徽标键是全新的设计。事实并非如此，因为它们几年前就已在部分 Chromebook 上首次亮相。不过，Googlebook 上确实有一项全新特性，可以说是直接照搬了 2014 年左右 Android 手机的设计。
配备这些按键并且在所有 Googlebook 上保持统一非常实用。在使用尚未针对桌面界面或鼠标控制进行深度优化的 Android 应用时，“返回”键有时显得尤为必要。我只是希望再次按下“主页”键能将所有应用恢复到原位，但那是另一项名为“桌面速览”（desktop peeking）的功能，对应的是不同的键盘快捷键。
如果你是当年的 Android 发烧友，看到这些按键重获新生会觉得颇有趣味。但它们同时也在提醒你，当 Android 系统暴露出它那些特有的毛病时，你有时确实需要一个兜底的应对方案。

aiStories.title: 微软发布搭载英伟达芯片的新款AI PC及改版Windows 11
aiStories.originalTitle: Microsoft releases new Nvidia-chip AI PCs with revamped Windows 11
aiStories.snippet: Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its Surface Laptop Ultra, AI PCs that run on Nvidia chips that are designed to run AI models and agents.
aiStories.fullContent:
Back in June, Nvidia announced that it had secured agreements with Microsoft and a host of other PC makers to develop AI- and agent-ready PCs for Windows based on its RTX Spark chip, but details on the machines were scant at the time.

On Wednesday, at an event held in San Francisco during the city’s Tech Week, Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its new Surface Laptop Ultra. The PC comes in two base models, one that starts at $2,600 and one with a more powerful chip that starts at $3,700. Prices rise from there with options for more memory and storage, up to $5,900. (Microsoft says the highest-end device is already out of stock.)

Microsoft also revealed its new workstation powered by the RTX Spark chip: the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, which starts priced at $6,000 and comes equipped with Microsoft dev tools like VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, WSL, and PowerShell 7.

The pitch for both this PC and workstation is that they are designed to run AI models on-device locally (and for free) with the CPU, GPU, unified memory, and other hardware modifications, like superior cooling, necessary to handle them.

Plus, they are running a revamped version of Windows 11 that includes a feature called “Execution Containers.” This makes it easier to sandbox AI agents, the company says. That feature will be available for all Windows 11 users, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at the event.

Nadella explained: “One of the things we realized in the last 3-4 years is that just having a model doesn’t do much for anything. You really do need to orchestrate, and you need to have memory outside of the model. You need to have this harnessed layer that is able to take multiple models plus context, plus memory, and the action space.”

He added that Microsoft is enabling that “not just for our apps but apps for anyone’s agent. That’s what the Windows platform is all about going forward.”

The devices are clearly aimed at developers, so much so that Microsoft is offering up to $1,000 off to people who trade in a MacBook Pro, as Macs have become a popular choice for developers and AI agent enthusiasts, particularly in Silicon Valley.

Still, these Surface PCs, with such powerful graphics processing, are also capable of content creation, video processing, and gaming, the company promises.

Microsoft wasn’t the only PC company to announce the specs for its new Nvidia-RTX Spark AI Windows PCs on Wednesday. Dell also announced the details of its previously announced Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition PC. It’s available for preorder now for a later October delivery at Best Buy, priced at $3,800.

早在今年6月，英伟达就宣布已与微软及多家其他PC制造商达成协议，共同开发基于其RTX Spark芯片、适用于Windows的AI及智能体就绪（agent-ready）PC，但当时关于这些设备的细节披露甚少。

周三，在旧金山科技周（Tech Week）期间举行的一场活动中，微软公布了其新款Surface Laptop Ultra的规格和售价。该PC提供两款基础机型，一款起售价为2,600美元，另一款搭载更强大芯片的机型起售价为3,700美元。若选择更大的内存和存储配置，价格还会进一步上涨，最高可达5,900美元。（微软表示最高配机型目前已告售罄。）

微软还展示了其搭载RTX Spark芯片的新款工作站：Surface RTX Spark Dev Box，起售价为6,000美元，并预装了VS Code、GitHub Copilot CLI、WSL和PowerShell 7等微软开发工具。

这款PC和工作站的核心卖点在于，它们经过专门设计，依托CPU、GPU、统一内存以及更优异的散热系统等应对AI工作负载所必需的硬件调整，能够在本地设备上（且免费）运行AI模型。

此外，它们运行着改版后的Windows 11系统，该系统包含一项名为“执行容器”（Execution Containers）的功能。微软表示，这使得对AI智能体进行沙盒隔离变得更加容易。微软首席执行官萨提亚·纳德拉（Satya Nadella）在活动中表示，该功能将面向所有Windows 11用户开放。

纳德拉解释道：“过去三四年里我们意识到的事情之一是，单纯拥有一个模型其实起不到太大作用。你确实需要进行编排，并且需要在模型外部拥有记忆。你需要这样一个受控层，能够将多个模型、上下文、记忆以及行动空间整合在一起。”

他补充说，微软不仅在为自己的应用程序启用这一功能，“而且在为任何人的智能体应用程序提供支持。这就是Windows平台未来的核心所在。”

这些设备显然是针对开发者打造的，微软甚至为以MacBook Pro换购的用户提供最高1,000美元的折扣，因为Mac已成为开发者和AI智能体爱好者的热门选择，尤其是在硅谷。

尽管如此，微软承诺，凭借如此强大的图形处理能力，这些Surface PC同样能够胜任内容创作、视频处理和游戏。

周三公布新款搭载英伟达RTX Spark的AI Windows PC规格的，并非只有微软一家。戴尔也公布了此前已宣布的Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition PC的详细信息。该产品现已在百思买（Best Buy）开启预购，起售价为3,800美元，将于10月晚些时候发货。

With GPT-6, the chatbot’s responses can include interactive responses directly inside your conversation.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

OpenAI is launching a new Intelligent UI feature in ChatGPT that allows the chatbot to answer your questions with interactive visuals. The update, which is rolling out to all users alongside GPT-6, gives ChatGPT the ability to combine a text response with diagrams, charts, forms, tappable buttons, and more.

In a blog post explaining the change, OpenAI says it trained GPT-6 when to generate interactive visuals over text, as well as how to format them in its response. An example shared by OpenAI shows how ChatGPT might show a diagram of a seven-speed bicycle if you ask about its design, complete with interactive buttons that highlight different parts.

Another shows how ChatGPT can teach you to play Mahjong by generating visuals of each tile and placing them into categories that you can scroll through. You can also ask ChatGPT to generate tools for different tasks, such as a retirement savings calculator, retro game, or bill splitter. It will then generate the tool in-line with its response.

OpenAI announced its first GPT-6 models last month, but now it’s bringing the Sol and Luna versions to ChatGPT. In addition to enabling Intelligent UI, OpenAI says its GPT-6 allows ChatGPT to perform better web searches and provide quicker, partial answers to users while it gathers information. The first array of laptops powered by Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip are designed to compete with high-end MacBook Pros — and they’ve got some high-end prices to match.

The flagship Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark laptops from Dell, Lenovo, MSI, HP, and Asus start as low as $2,599 for configurations with an 18-core CPU, 24GB of unified memory, and 512GB of storage. That’s close in price to a similarly specced 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro chip, though Apple includes 1TB of storage. But the prices for both RTX Spark and Apple laptops of course go much, much higher.

Of the pricing we’ve seen so far, a kitted-out Asus ProArt P16 RTX Spark laptop with a 20-core chip, 128GB of unified memory, and 2TB of storage costs up to $6,999.99. We don’t yet know the full breadth of configuration options for Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra, as the preorder page only has an email sign-up box to get updates, but a 48GB model on Best Buy costs $3,999.99.

Wildly expensive laptops aren’t really anything new: you can configure a 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Max chip to nearly $10,000 if you max out all options. But the first volley of RTX Spark options are obviously aimed at the high-end side of creators and local AI users. And RAMageddon certainly isn’t helping make this any easier on peoples’ wallets.

Will they be worth it? We’ll find out soon. The Surface Laptop Ultra and other RTX Spark laptops are launching this month — as early as October 16th.

aiStories.title: 要闻：今天，我们很高兴宣布 Claude Haiku 5.5 在 Amazon Bedrock 以及 AWS 上的 C
aiStories.source: AWS Machine Learning Blog (亚马逊云科技官方英文)
aiStories.snippet: Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. According to Anthropic, it is the fastest, most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for subagents and high-volume, cost-sensitive work, and costs around 75% less than Claude Haiku 4.5 for most tasks. This post covers its improvements and how to get started.
aiStories.fullContent:
Today, we’re excited to announce the availability of Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS . According to Anthropic, Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest and most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for subagents and high-volume, cost-sensitive work. It also costs around 75 percent less than Claude Haiku 4.5 for most tasks.

Amazon Bedrock gives you Haiku 5.5 capabilities while keeping your data within AWS infrastructure with Regional data residency. It works with the AWS controls your team already uses, including AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) for access, AWS CloudTrail for audit, Amazon CloudWatch for monitoring, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Usage appears on your AWS bill.

Claude Platform on AWS gives you direct access to Anthropic’s native platform experience and capabilities through the AWS Management Console. Build, test, and deploy with the same APIs, features, and console experience you’d get working with Anthropic directly, unified with AWS billing and authentication.

This post covers Claude Haiku 5.5’s improvements, practical guidance on when to choose Haiku 5.5, and how to get started on Amazon Bedrock.

What makes Claude Haiku 5.5 different

Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic’s most capable Haiku model, across coding, tool use, computer use, and agentic tasks. It’s also the first Haiku model with effort controls, so you can tune cost against intelligence for each task instead of picking one setting for an entire workload.

The improvements stand out on quick and repeatable work at scale. For coding tasks, it acts as a subagent routing requests, reviewing code and classifying long documents. For knowledge work, Haiku 5.5 pulls key information from small-to-medium documents, does initial scans, and answers quick questions over a knowledge base. For interactive applications, it responds fast enough for simple conversations to have quick and helpful answers. It also handles traditional natural language processing (NLP) tasks such as classification, summarization, and text generation at the volume and cost that production features require.

Haiku 5.5 handles agentic coding and multi-step tool use, and supports high-resolution images. Haiku 5.5 can be used as a strong computer use subagent for repetitive browser and desktop tasks, at a cost that holds up at scale. In development workflows, it’s a good fit for iterating quickly on UI and UX changes and for small, specific code base changes across multiple files.

Pairing Claude Haiku 5.5 with Opus 5.5

Haiku 5.5 pairs with the recently announced Claude Opus 5.5. Together, they make a strong team: Opus 5.5 plans and makes the judgment calls, and Haiku 5.5 carries out well-defined tasks quickly and at scale. You get careful reasoning where it counts and lower cost and latency everywhere.

Claude Opus 5.5 plans the work and makes the judgment calls. It breaks down complex problems, decides the approach, and takes on the hardest reasoning, such as release debugging, security review of large pull requests, and long analyses that end in a finished report.

Claude Haiku 5.5 takes on the fast layer of subagents. It handles quick, high-volume tasks, such as routing requests, classifying and summarizing, rewriting long documents, and applying small, specific changes across many files. As a review subagent, it can quickly check the order of operations and high-level direction, so Opus 5.5 can spend its tokens on the hardest reasoning. Because it is fast and cost efficient, you can run many Haiku subagents in parallel.

Getting started with Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock

To try Haiku 5.5, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , then Playground , and select Haiku 5.5 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it.

Figure 1: Selecting an Anthropic Claude model in the Amazon Bedrock console Playground

Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime through the Anthropic SDK. You can also use the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK .

You must have the following prerequisites:

Active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.

AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) installed and configured.

Boto3 installed: pip install boto3 .

Anthropic SDK installed: pip install anthropic .

The Amazon Bedrock Token Generator for Amazon Bedrock authentication installed: pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator .

AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions: bedrock:InvokeModel , bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream .

Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) with the InvokeModel API:

import boto3 import json

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1" )

# Invoke Claude Haiku 5.5 response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model( modelId="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5", contentType="application/json", accept="application/json", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] }) )

result = json.loads(response["body"].read()) # Haiku 5.5 may return a thinking block before the text block, # so select the text block rather than a fixed index. print(next(b["text"] for b in result["content"] if b["type"] == "text"))

You can also use the Amazon Bedrock Converse API for a unified multi-model experience:

# Create a Bedrock Runtime client bedrock_runtime = boto3.client( service_name="bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1" )

# Invoke Claude Haiku 5.5 response = bedrock_runtime.converse( modelId="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5", messages=[ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "text": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?" } ] } ], inferenceConfig={ "maxTokens": 4096 } )

if 'output' in response: blocks = response['output']['message']['content'] print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))

You can also use the Anthropic Messages API through the anthropic SDK package for a streamlined experience:

from anthropic import Anthropic from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token

token = provide_token(region="us-east-1")

client = Anthropic( base_url="https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/anthropic", api_key=token, )

# Invoke Claude Haiku 5.5 response = client.messages.create( model="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5", max_tokens=1024, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}], ) print(response)

You can explore the Getting Started notebook for more examples. You can monitor usage, performance, and costs through Amazon CloudWatch and AWS Cost Explorer to scale your applications as demand grows.

Claude Haiku 5.5 is available today on Amazon Bedrock through the US Geo CRIS (us.), EU Geo CRIS (eu.), AU Geo CRIS (au.), JP Geo CRIS (jp.) and Global CRIS (global.) inference profiles on bedrock-runtime . In AWS GovCloud (US), it’s available on both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints.

See the Amazon Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported AWS Regions. For pricing information, see Amazon Bedrock pricing . It’s also available through Claude Platform on AWS in North America

Give Claude Haiku 5.5 a try on the Amazon Bedrock console , in Claude Platform on AWS , or explore the Getting Started notebooks on GitHub.

Aamna is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI focusing on Anthropic models and operationalizing and governing generative AI systems at scale on Amazon Bedrock. She helps ISVs solve their challenges, embrace innovation, and create new business opportunities with Amazon Bedrock.

Dani is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI at AWS, working on go-to-market for Anthropic on Amazon Bedrock. He helps enterprises across the world design and deploy generative AI solutions using Anthropic’s models and capabilities on Amazon Bedrock to build scalable, production-ready applications.

Alfredo is a Senior Specialist Solutions Architect for Generative AI at AWS, focusing on Anthropic models go-to-market on Amazon Bedrock. He works with Financial Services customers to design and scale generative AI solutions across distributed systems and turn generative AI experiments into production workloads. Outside of work, he is passionate about family and endurance sports.

Sofian is a technology leader with over 12 years of experience building AI solutions, and leading high-performing teams to maximize customer outcomes. He is passionate about empowering diverse talents to drive global impact and achieve their career aspirations.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
今天，我们很高兴宣布 Claude Haiku 5.5 在 Amazon Bedrock 以及 AWS 上的 Claude Platform 正式上线。Anthropic 表示，Claude Haiku 5.5 是 Claude 5.5 家族中速度最快、效率最高的模型，专为子智能体（subagents）以及大规模、对成本敏感的任务打造。在大多数任务中，其成本比 Claude Haiku 4.5 低约 75%。

Amazon Bedrock 在赋予你 Haiku 5.5 能力的同时，可凭借区域数据驻留（Regional data residency）将你的数据安全保留在 AWS 基础设施内。它能无缝对接团队现有的 AWS 管控体系，包括用于访问控制的 AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)、用于审计的 AWS CloudTrail、用于监控的 Amazon CloudWatch 以及 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails。所有用量均统一体现在你的 AWS 账单中。

AWS 上的 Claude Platform 则允许你通过 AWS 管理控制台直接体验 Anthropic 原生平台功能与能力。你可以使用与直接对接 Anthropic 完全相同的 API、功能和控制台体验进行构建、测试和部署，同时统一接入 AWS 的计费与身份验证。

本文将介绍 Claude Haiku 5.5 的多项改进、选择 Haiku 5.5 的实用建议，以及如何在 Amazon Bedrock 上快速上手。

### Claude Haiku 5.5 的独特之处

Claude Haiku 5.5 是 Anthropic 迄今能力最强的 Haiku 模型，涵盖编码、工具调用、计算机操作（computer use）和智能体任务。它也是首个具备精力/努力程度控制（effort controls）的 Haiku 模型，允许你针对每个任务在成本与智能水平之间进行平衡微调，而无需在整个工作负载中使用同一种配置。

这些改进在规模化、快速且可重复的工作中尤为突出。在编码任务中，它可作为子智能体进行请求路由、代码审查和长文档分类。在知识密集型工作中，Haiku 5.5 能从中小型文档中提取核心信息、执行初步扫描，并基于知识库快速作答。在交互式应用中，其响应极为敏捷，足以支持简单会话并给出快速实用的回答。它还能够以满足生产环境所需的通量与成本要求，处理分类、摘要和文本生成等传统自然语言处理（NLP）任务。

Haiku 5.5 支持智能体编码和多步骤工具调用，并支持高分辨率图像。Haiku 5.5 还可作为一个强大的计算机操作子智能体，以能够在大规模场景下持续维持的低成本，处理重复性的浏览器和桌面任务。在开发工作流中，它非常适合对 UI 和 UX 变更进行快速迭代，以及跨多个文件执行细小、具体的代码库修改。

### Claude Haiku 5.5 与 Opus 5.5 协同组合

Haiku 5.5 可与近期发布的 Claude Opus 5.5 协同工作。两者构成了强有力的组合：Opus 5.5 负责规划与关键决策判断，Haiku 5.5 则快速且规模化地执行定义清晰的具体任务。这样你既能在关键环节获得严密推理，又能在全局降低成本与延迟。

Claude Opus 5.5 负责规划整体工作并作出决策判断。它能分解复杂问题、敲定方案路线，并承担最繁重的推理工作，例如发布调试、大型 PR 的安全审查以及生成最终报告的长篇分析。

Claude Haiku 5.5 则承担快速响应的子智能体层。它负责处理快速、高通量的任务，如请求路由、分类与摘要、重写长文档，以及跨多个文件应用细微且具体的更改。作为审查子智能体，它可以迅速核验操作顺序和宏观方向，从而让 Opus 5.5 将其 token 资源集中用于难度最高的推理上。得益于其出色的速度与成本效益，你可以并行运行大量 Haiku 子智能体。

### 在 Amazon Bedrock 上快速上手 Claude Haiku 5.5

若要体验 Haiku 5.5，请打开 Amazon Bedrock 控制台，依次选择 Test（测试）、Playground（试验场），并将模型选择为 Haiku 5.5。接下来即可直接输入 Prompt 进行测试。

图 1：在 Amazon Bedrock 控制台 Playground 中选择 Anthropic Claude 模型

在代码层面，你可以通过 Anthropic SDK 调用针对 bedrock-runtime 的 Anthropic Messages API 来访问该模型。你也可以通过 AWS 命令行界面（AWS CLI）及 AWS SDK，调用 bedrock-runtime 上的 Invoke 和 Converse API。

使用前需满足以下先决条件：
- 拥有已开通 Amazon Bedrock 访问权限的有效 AWS 账户。
- 安装并配置好 AWS 命令行界面（AWS CLI）。
- 安装 Boto3：`pip install boto3`。
- 安装 Anthropic SDK：`pip install anthropic`。
- 安装用于 Amazon Bedrock 身份验证的 Amazon Bedrock Token Generator：`pip install aws_bedrock_token_generator`。
- 具备 AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) 权限：`bedrock:InvokeModel`、`bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`。

以下是使用适用于 Python 的 AWS SDK (Boto3) 调用 InvokeModel API 的快速示例：

```python
import boto3
import json

# 创建 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client(
    service_name="bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1"
)

# 调用 Claude Haiku 5.5
response = bedrock_runtime.invoke_model(
    modelId="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5",
    contentType="application/json",
    accept="application/json",
    body=json.dumps({
        "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31",
        "max_tokens": 4096,
        "messages": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"
            }
        ]
    })
)

result = json.loads(response["body"].read())
# Haiku 5.5 可能会在文本块之前返回思考块（thinking block），
# 因此需选择文本块而非使用固定索引。
print(next(b["text"] for b in result["content"] if b["type"] == "text"))
```

你还可以使用 Amazon Bedrock Converse API 获得统一的多模型调用体验：

```python
# 创建 Bedrock Runtime 客户端
bedrock_runtime = boto3.client(
    service_name="bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1"
)

# 调用 Claude Haiku 5.5
response = bedrock_runtime.converse(
    modelId="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "text": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"
                }
            ]
        }
    ],
    inferenceConfig={
        "maxTokens": 4096
    }
)

if 'output' in response:
    blocks = response['output']['message']['content']
    print('\n'.join(b.get('text', '') for b in blocks if 'text' in b))
```

你同样可以通过 anthropic SDK 软件包使用 Anthropic Messages API，享受更为简化的接入体验：

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic
from aws_bedrock_token_generator import provide_token

token = provide_token(region="us-east-1")

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/anthropic",
    api_key=token,
)

# 调用 Claude Haiku 5.5
response = client.messages.create(
    model="global.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Can you explain the features of Amazon Bedrock?"}],
)
print(response)
```

你可以查阅《快速入门指南》（Getting Started）Notebook 获取更多示例。随着业务需求增长，你可以借助 Amazon CloudWatch 和 AWS Cost Explorer 监控使用量、性能和成本，以便从容扩展应用规模。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

ICANN’s latest top-level domain applications are out, and they are all about AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by David Pierce

For the first time in years, the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers — better known as ICANN — is accepting applications for new top-level domains. These are the suffixes at the end of all URLs, and you may know them as things like .com, .org, and .pizza.

ICANN just announced the 1,615 applications that have been submitted so far, from 481 different applicants. The trend will not surprise you: AI is everywhere. Ten different companies, including both Meta and OpenAI, applied for the .agent domain. Seven, including OpenAI, applied for .agi. Six, including OpenAI, applied for .asi, clearly attempting to get in on President Trump’s demand to switch from “artificial intelligence” to “super intelligence.” Four companies applied for .intelligence, and Meta is one of two interested in the preposterously long .superintelligence. (OpenAI applied for a total of 15 TLDs; Meta wants a whopping 21.)

There are, broadly, two types of domains in these applications. One is more generic, the kind of thing lots of people or companies might use. There are hundreds of those in this current batch, from .geek to .haha to .anime to .jackpot. There’s also my personal favorite new one, .itiswhatitis.

The other is purely branded, giving a company its own TLD to use for its own purposes. There are 345 brand applications in this batch, including everything from .applebees and .bankofamerica to .zillow and .zoom. Meta applied for .facebook, .instagram, .messenger, .meta, .frommeta, and .threads, which it could use for many purposes; Bluesky applied for .bsky with the apparent intention of weaving the domain into its usernames; OpenAI applied for .chatgpt, .codex, .openai, .gpt, and others; Anthropic wants .anthropic and .claude. These strings could ultimately make for memorable product pages, social media usernames, and much more besides.

It has mostly been a tough road for these alternate TLDs over the last few years. Some, like .ai or .app, have become somewhat popular thanks to various tech trends, but most people just never got used to the idea of typing .restaurant or .babysitting, and .com and a few others have actually become more important than ever. It’s interesting to see so many brands go for their own domain, which only Google and a few others have accomplished before.

This is but one step in the process of creating a new top-level domain, and nothing will be made official before sometime next year. But it appears that even as the world becomes more filled with and mediated by AI, great domain names continue to matter. Even the AI companies think so.

多年来，互联网名称与数字地址分配机构（更广为人知的名称是 ICANN）首次开放新顶级域名的申请。顶级域名即所有网址末尾的后缀，你可能熟悉的有 .com、.org 和 .pizza 等。

ICANN 刚刚公布了迄今为止提交的 1615 份申请，分别来自 481 家不同的申请机构。其趋势并不令人意外：AI 无处不在。包括 Meta 和 OpenAI 在内的 10 家不同公司申请了 .agent 域名。包括 OpenAI 在内的 7 家机构申请了 .agi。包括 OpenAI 在内的 6 家机构申请了 .asi，这显然是在迎合特朗普总统提出的将“人工智能（artificial intelligence）”改称为“超级智能（super intelligence）”的要求。4 家公司申请了 .intelligence，而 Meta 则是对长得离谱的 .superintelligence 感兴趣的两家公司之一。（OpenAI 共申请了 15 个顶级域名；Meta 更是高达惊人的 21 个。）

粗略来看，这些申请中的域名主要分为两类。一类偏通用，属于许多个人或公司都可能使用的类型。在本批申请中有数百个此类域名，从 .geek、.haha、.anime 到 .jackpot 不一而足。还有我个人最喜欢的一个新域名：.itiswhatitis（意为“木已成舟/顺其自然”）。

另一类则是纯品牌域名，赋予公司专属于自己的顶级域名以供自身使用。这一批中共有 345 个品牌申请，涵盖了从 .applebees 和 .bankofamerica 到 .zillow 和 .zoom 的一切。Meta 申请了 .facebook、.instagram、.messenger、.meta、.frommeta 以及 .threads，这些域名可用于多种场景；Bluesky 申请了 .bsky，显然打算将该域名融入其用户名体系；OpenAI 申请了 .chatgpt、.codex、.openai、.gpt 等；Anthropic 则想要 .anthropic 和 .claude。这些字符最终有望打造出令人难忘的产品页面、社交媒体用户名以及更多应用。

在过去几年里，这些备选顶级域名的发展历程大多颇为坎坷。受各种科技潮流推动，诸如 .ai 或 .app 等部分域名变得相当受欢迎，但大多数人根本没有习惯去输入形如 .restaurant 或 .babysitting 这样的后缀，而 .com 等少数几个顶级域名实际上反而变得比以往任何时候都更加重要。看到如此多的品牌争相打造自己的专属域名，着实颇有意思，而此前只有谷歌等少数几家企业做到过这一点。

这仅仅是创建新顶级域名流程中的一步，在明年某个时候之前不会有任何定论。但事实表明，即便世界日益充斥着 AI 并受其调控，优质的域名依然举足轻重。就连那些 AI 公司自己也是这么认为的。

Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface-focused keynote in San Francisco.

The biggest announcement was arguably the release details about the Surface Laptop Ultra , its new laptop that’s powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm-based chip. The machine will start at $2,599 for a configuration with an 8-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage, and it will be released on October 16th. The laptop also has built-in magnetic USB-C charging instead of the proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging port. The Verge ‘s Tom Warren published a deep dive all about the new laptop . Microsoft also announced that the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a mini PC for developers, is available for preorder for $5,999 ahead of shipping in November.

In addition, Microsoft shared details about some updates coming to Windows , including “Hybrid Intelligence” features that lets Copilot use files on your Windows PC to take actions and a new search experience that lets you do quick actions from the search bar.

You can catch up with all of our coverage from the event right here.

aiStories.title: 借助 Amazon Quick 与 Amazon Bedrock 重新审视 RAG 的访问控制
aiStories.originalTitle: Rethinking access control for RAG with Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock
aiStories.source: AWS Machine Learning Blog (亚马逊云科技官方英文)
aiStories.snippet: Enterprise RAG unlocks insights from knowledge sources like SharePoint, Google Drive, and Confluence, but those sources carry complex permissions. Learn how Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases enforce document-level access controls in real time, verifying permissions directly with authoritative sources at query time.
aiStories.fullContent:
Enterprise organizations are adopting Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) to unlock insights from company knowledge sources like Microsoft SharePoint, Google Drive, and Atlassian Confluence. However, these knowledge sources contain sensitive information governed by complex permission structures. Making sure that AI-generated answers respect those permissions is one of the hardest challenges in enterprise AI.

In this post, we explore how Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases solve this challenge through real-time access control list (ACL) enforcement, verifying permissions directly with authoritative sources at query time.

Consider this scenario: A SharePoint site owner creates a knowledge base for their organization. Team members across multiple departments use an AI assistant to get answers from this knowledge base. The critical requirement is that each team member must only receive AI-generated insights from documents they’re authorized to access.

This is a universal enterprise challenge. Organizations want to democratize access to AI-powered insights without compromising their existing security posture. A single unauthorized document surfaced in an AI response could expose confidential strategy documents, unreleased financial data, or sensitive HR information.

Why existing approaches fall short

A common approach to RAG access control uses a replicate-and-filter approach to enforce document-level permissions. Here’s how it typically works:

A data source connector (for example, SharePoint connector) pulls ACLs as part of a periodic sync job.

The ACLs are replicated from the data source and stored as attributes in an index.

At query time, the AI system maps the logged-in user to the stored ACL attributes and filters results accordingly.

While this approach seems reasonable on the surface, it has three fundamental weaknesses.

Problem 1: The AI system isn’t the source of truth

In this model, the AI system takes sole responsibility for enforcement without being the authoritative source of permissions. This requires data connectors to accurately replicate complex, source-specific ACL logic across various data sources. Each data source has its own unique permission models. Mapping inheritance hierarchies, group memberships, conditional access policies, and deny rules across dozens of connectors is an error-prone undertaking.

Problem 2: Stale permissions create security gaps

In general, data connectors support pull-based syncs that run on demand or on a customer-defined schedule. The ACLs in these AI solutions are a snapshot in time from when the last sync ran. Some solutions use event-based updates, but this doesn’t work universally. For example, a data source like Confluence doesn’t emit an event when group membership changes. Between syncs, a user who had their access revoked might still receive AI answers from documents they should no longer see.

Problem 3: Evolving data source capabilities

Data sources regularly change or introduce new mechanisms to control access to content. A new permission feature in SharePoint or a change to the Google Drive sharing model could create gaps in the ACL mapping logic. This can expose content until the connector is updated.

How AWS solves this: Real-time ACL enforcement

To address these challenges, we implemented real-time ACL checks as an additional layer of security on top of existing pre-retrieval ACL filtering for Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. This makes sure the system enforces the most current access controls by checking permissions directly with the authoritative source at query time. This avoids relying on potentially stale or incorrectly mapped ACL data.

Architecture overview

The following diagram illustrates our hybrid approach that delivers both semantic search performance and real-time security capabilities.

Figure 1: Real-time ACL enforcement architecture for Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, combining pre-retrieval filtering (Stage 1) with real-time verification against authoritative sources (Stage 2)

How it works: A Google Drive example

When a user submits a query to an Amazon Quick agent that uses a Google Drive knowledge base, the system enforces access controls in two stages:

Stage 1: Pre-retrieval filtering

Amazon Quick performs a semantic search against the vector index to find the most relevant document passages. The system applies access control lists that are already stored in the index. This produces a preliminary set of candidate documents. This stage is necessary because real-time API calls for every document in the index would be too costly at scale.

Stage 2: Real-time verification

Amazon Quick verifies the candidate documents in real time by calling the Google Drive APIs. It uses the service account credential that the administrator provided to generate user-specific access tokens through impersonation. Google Drive maintains the source of truth for access control lists associated with each document. Documents the user is not authorized to access are excluded from the retrieved result set. Only the verified and authorized document passages are passed to the large language model (LLM) as context. The model uses this knowledge to generate a response.

This two-stage approach balances performance with security. It uses cached ACLs for efficiency while facilitating correctness through real-time checks. In addition to ACL enforcement, Amazon Bedrock provides responsible AI controls. These include Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for content filtering, grounding checks to reduce hallucinations, and configurable safety policies to help organizations deploy generative AI applications responsibly.

Why this matters for your organization

This approach delivers three key benefits:

Always-current permissions – No more security gaps between sync cycles when you are using a RAG product. If an employee’s access is revoked, the change is reflected in AI responses within moments, not hours or days.

Confidence to scale – Organizations can expand their knowledge base coverage knowing that real-time ACL checks verify permissions with the authoritative source for every query, regardless of data source.

Reduced operational burden – You don’t need to worry about sync frequency.

What customers are saying about this

“When we set out to evaluate AI solutions for our organization, our security and compliance teams were clear about their top priority: ensuring that colleagues would only ever see information they’re authorized to access. It’s a fundamental requirement, but one that many platforms struggle to address in a meaningful way. Amazon Quick’s approach to real-time access control answered that question definitively and demonstrated a level of rigor that stood out throughout our evaluation. It gave our internal review board the confidence to move forward and set a strong foundation for how we think about AI governance going forward.”

— Jamahl Wiggins, Sr. Specialist – M365 Innovation, Mondelēz International

Mondelēz International has deployed Amazon Quick for their over 35,000 employees across four regions.

In this post, we talked about how Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases implement real-time ACL enforcement to solve a critical security challenge for enterprises. The dual-layer ACL architecture verifies permissions directly with authoritative sources at query time. This makes sure AI-generated answers include only content a user is authorized to access.

To get started, visit Amazon Quick and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases .

Amit is the Principal Product Manager for knowledge bases for Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Quick. His work enables secure AI interactions grounded in enterprise knowledge, transforming how organizations use their data for AI-powered insights and decision-making. He was the product manager who pioneered this real-time access control feature from 0 to 1.

Suren is a Generative AI Specialist Solutions Architect at AWS on the Amazon Quick service team, where he helps enterprises build secure, agentic AI grounded in their own knowledge. He works at the frontier of agent-to-agent (A2A) orchestration and Model Context Protocol (MCP) action connectors – the pieces that let AI agents reason across tools, take real actions, and securely tap enterprise knowledge rather than just answer questions.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
企业组织正在采用检索增强生成（RAG），以挖掘来自微软 SharePoint、谷歌云端硬盘（Google Drive）以及 Atlassian Confluence 等公司知识源的洞察。然而，这些知识源包含受复杂权限结构监管的敏感信息。确保人工智能生成的答案遵循这些权限，是企业级人工智能面临的最大挑战之一。

在本文中，我们将探讨 Amazon Quick 和 Amazon Bedrock 知识库（Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases）如何通过实时访问控制列表（ACL）执行来解决这一挑战，即在查询时直接向权威源验证权限。

试想这样一个场景：某 SharePoint 站点所有者为其组织创建了一个知识库。跨多个部门的团队成员使用人工智能助手从该知识库中获取答案。关键要求在于，每位团队成员只能接收来自其有权访问文档的人工智能洞察。

这是一个普遍存在的企业挑战。组织希望在不妥协现有安全态势的前提下，普及对人工智能驱动洞察的访问。人工智能回答中只要出现一篇未经授权的文档，就可能暴露机密战略文件、未公开的财务数据或敏感的人力资源信息。

为什么现有方法存在不足

RAG 访问控制的常见做法是采用“复制并过滤”方法来执行文档级权限。其典型工作原理如下：
数据源连接器（例如 SharePoint 连接器）在执行定期同步作业时拉取 ACL。
ACL 从数据源复制出来，并作为属性存储在索引中。
在查询时，人工智能系统将登录用户与存储的 ACL 属性进行映射，并相应地过滤结果。

虽然这种方法表面上看起来很合理，但它存在三个根本缺陷。

问题 1：人工智能系统并非权威事实来源（Source of Truth）
在这种模型中，人工智能系统承担了执行的全部职责，但自身却并非权限的权威源。这要求数据连接器在各种数据源之间准确复制复杂的、特定于源的 ACL 逻辑。每个数据源都有其独特的权限模型。在数十个连接器之间映射继承层次结构、组成员身份、条件访问策略和拒绝规则是一项极易出错的工作。

问题 2：过期权限引发安全隐患
通常，数据连接器支持基于拉取的同步，这些同步按需运行或按客户定义的计划运行。这些人工智能解决方案中的 ACL 只是上次同步运行时的快照。某些解决方案使用基于事件的更新，但该方法并不能通用。例如，像 Confluence 这样的数据源在组成员身份发生变更时并不会发出事件。在两次同步之间，已被撤销访问权限的用户仍可能收到来自他们不再应该看到的文档的人工智能回答。

问题 3：数据源功能不断演进
数据源会定期更改或引入控制内容访问的新机制。SharePoint 中的新权限功能或 Google Drive 共享模型的变更可能会导致 ACL 映射逻辑出现盲区。在连接器更新之前，这可能会使内容面临泄露风险。

AWS 如何解决这一问题：实时 ACL 执行
为了应对这些挑战，我们在 Amazon Quick 和 Amazon Bedrock 知识库现有的检索前 ACL 过滤之上，实施了实时 ACL 检查作为附加安全层。这确保了系统在查询时直接向权威源检查权限，从而执行最新的访问控制。这避免了依赖可能已过时或映射不正确的 ACL 数据。

架构概述
下图展示了我们的混合方法，该方法既能提供语义搜索性能，又能提供实时安全保障能力。
图 1：Amazon Quick 和 Amazon Bedrock 知识库的实时 ACL 执行架构，将检索前过滤（阶段 1）与针对权威源的实时验证（阶段 2）相结合。

工作原理：以 Google Drive 为例
当用户向使用 Google Drive 知识库的 Amazon Quick 代理提交查询时，系统分两个阶段执行访问控制：

阶段 1：检索前过滤
Amazon Quick 对向量索引执行语义搜索，以找到最相关的文档段落。系统应用已存储在索引中的访问控制列表。这将生成一组初步的候选文档。这一阶段是必要的，因为在海量规模下对索引中的每篇文档都进行实时 API 调用成本过高。

阶段 2：实时验证
Amazon Quick 通过调用 Google Drive API 实时验证候选文档。它使用管理员提供的服务账号凭据，通过模拟（impersonation）生成特定于用户的访问令牌。Google Drive 保留着与每篇文档关联的访问控制列表的权威事实来源。未授权用户访问的文档将从检索结果集中排除。只有经过验证且获得授权的文档段落才会作为上下文传递给大语言模型（LLM）。该模型利用这些知识生成回答。

这种两阶段方法平衡了性能与安全性。它使用缓存的 ACL 确保效率，同时通过实时检查促进准确性。除了 ACL 执行外，Amazon Bedrock 还提供负责任的人工智能控制。其中包括用于内容过滤的 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails、用于减少幻觉的基础事实检查（grounding checks），以及可配置的安全策略，以帮助组织负责任地部署生成式人工智能应用程序。

为什么这对您的组织至关重要
这种方法带来了三大核心优势：
权限时刻保持最新 —— 使用 RAG 产品时，同步周期之间不再存在安全隐患。如果某位员工的访问权限被撤销，该变更会在几秒钟内在人工智能回答中生效，而不是几小时或几天。
放心扩展 —— 无论数据源为何，组织在扩展知识库覆盖范围时都能确信：每次查询都会通过权威源对权限进行实时 ACL 检查。
降低运维负担 —— 您无需再为同步频率而操心。

客户评价
“当我们着手为组织评估人工智能解决方案时，我们的安全与合规团队明确了他们的首要任务：确保同事只能看到他们被授权访问的信息。这是一项基本要求，但许多平台很难以有意义的方式予以解决。Amazon Quick 的实时访问控制方法明确解答了这一问题，并在我们的整个评估过程中展现出了出类拔萃的严谨性。它让我们的内部审查委员会充满信心推进项目，并为我们未来思考人工智能治理奠定了坚实的基础。”

—— Jamahl Wiggins，亿滋国际（Mondelēz International）M365 创新高级专员

亿滋国际已为其分布在四个大区的超过 35,000 名员工部署了 Amazon Quick。

在本文中，我们探讨了 Amazon Quick 和 Amazon Bedrock 知识库（Knowledge Bases）如何通过实施实时访问控制列表（ACL）强制执行，解决企业面临的关键安全挑战。双层 ACL 架构在查询时直接与权威来源验证权限。这确保了 AI 生成的答案仅包含用户有权访问的内容。

欲开始使用，请访问 Amazon Quick 和 Amazon Bedrock 知识库。

Amit 是 Amazon Bedrock 和 Amazon Quick 知识库业务的首席产品经理。他的工作致力于实现基于企业知识的安全 AI 交互，转变企业利用自身数据进行 AI 驱动洞察与决策的方式。他是从 0 到 1 开创这一实时访问控制功能的产品经理。

Suren 是 AWS Amazon Quick 服务团队的生成式 AI 专业解决方案架构师，负责协助企业构建基于自身知识的安全、智能体式（agentic）AI。他致力于智能体间（A2A）编排和模型上下文协议（MCP）操作连接器等前沿领域——这些关键组件使 AI 智能体能够跨工具进行推理、采取实际操作并安全地调取企业知识，而不仅仅是回答问题。

aiStories.title: 移动端亮相仅一个月后，Meta的Muse助手正式登陆iPad
aiStories.originalTitle: Meta’s Muse launches on iPad just a month after its mobile debut
aiStories.snippet: Meta’s AI agent Muse is now available on iPad, just a month after its mobile debut, as the company rapidly expands the assistant’s reach and integrations.
aiStories.fullContent:
If there’s any doubt about how seriously Meta is taking AI, here’s a new signal: The company on Wednesday announced that its Muse assistant is now available in a dedicated iPad app. That’s a milestone it took Instagram some 15 years to reach, despite constant user demand.

Muse, meanwhile, hit the iPad just a month after launching on iPhone.

(To be fair, it may not be as difficult to bring something like Muse to iPad, given its text-heavy interface, where image and video resolution and formatting matter less.)

Since launching on iOS and Android on September 8, Muse has topped 6.6 million installs, according to estimates from market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. The app, which is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents, lets users connect their accounts to stay on top of email, meetings, bills, and more, and to complete tasks like booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases.

To make that work, Meta has been adding partners in the effort, which appear in Muse as “connectors.” Users can add and sign in to them selectively, depending on which parts of their online life they’re comfortable letting an AI agent handle.

With the iPad release, Meta has updated this list with several of its newer additions, including connectors aimed at small businesses, like Asana, Canva, Dropbox, Figma, QuickBooks, GitHub, Klaviyo, and Zoom, as well as connectors for Meta ad accounts. It also added Notion and Granola.

In addition, Meta recently announced more retail partners, like Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart, and Wayfair. These allow the agent to shop those retailers’ sites and complete transactions on users’ behalf. Because this technology is still new, these experiences can still run into issues as websites mistake agents for bots and block their access.

On Tuesday, Meta announced that it’s working with industry partners on a technological solution to this problem in the form of an open standard that would allow personal AI agents to identify themselves to businesses. That would help businesses sort the good bots from the bad.

trendStories.title: 我已经被谷歌取消收录了
trendStories.fullContent:
I don't remember exactly when but, earlier in the year, I decided I didn't want this website to be indexed by search engines anymore. A lot of it has to do with AI and the relentless scraping that plagues the internet now. I know that as long as my blog is accessible by the public internet, there are no real measures I can put in to stop it but at least some of it will be respected.

I started out by setting a blanket disallow in the robots.txt.

When I realised that didn't do anything after a few weeks of waiting and checking, I set the robots meta tag.

I thought that would do the trick. What I didn't realise is that you have to actually, ironically, allow the bot that will do the deindexing to visit your website so that it can see the meta tag that tells it to not index your page anymore.

I also did this with several other common bots and removed them from the robots.txt whenever I found that my website had been deindexed.

It's been at least 3 months since I did my last change to have Google deindex me and, after checking today, I'm happy to announce that this website is free from Google! 🥳
trendStories.fullTranslation:
我不记得具体是什么时候了，但在今年早些时候，我决定不再希望这个网站被搜索引擎收录。这在很大程度上与人工智能以及如今困扰互联网的无休止抓取有关。我知道，只要我的博客能被公共互联网访问，就没有什么真正的方法能阻止它，但至少有一部分规则会得到遵守。

我一开始是在 robots.txt 中设置了全局禁止访问（blanket disallow）。

在等待并检查了几周后，当我发现这并没有起任何作用时，我设置了 robots 元标签（meta tag）。

我以为这样就行了。但我当时没有意识到的是，讽刺的是，你实际上必须允许负责取消收录的爬虫访问你的网站，这样它才能看到那条告知它不再收录你页面的元标签。

我还对其他几款常见的爬虫进行了同样的操作，每当发现自己的网站已被取消收录时，就将它们从 robots.txt 中移除。

距离我为了让谷歌取消收录而做出最后一次更改已经过去了至少 3 个月，在今天检查之后，我很高兴地宣布，这个网站终于摆脱谷歌了！🥳

trendStories.title: 一篇关于 API 的吐槽
trendStories.fullContent:
I have had the displeasure of integrating with a few different APIs over the past few weeks while working to automate Vori’s onboarding flow. These APIs have been for systems including contract rendering and e-signature collection, invoicing/billing systems, CRMs, card processors and gateways, and card terminal providers.

They all kinda suck in their own ways. This would be somewhat acceptable if they were doing novel work in new fields, but these are all APIs for solutions that have existed for a decade or more. It’s also frustrating because the developers could simply copy existing, better, APIs and practices, and come out ahead!

Here are some of my pet peeves.

You’ve already messed up if I need to log in to read your API documentation. Kudos for actually writing the docs, but why do I need to log in!? I have to interrupt my flow to fill out a form or send an email to your support team, and wait a few hours or days, just to read documentation!?

I complained to one team about this and they agreed that gated documentation is not ideal. However, an executive wanted lead tracking. WTF!? We are already customers. The lead is closed-won. There’s nothing else to track!

This is worse with agentic development. I prefer to provide links to docs so the agent can explore the schema, build a client, and integrate. That flow is disrupted by gating. I now have to download the docs in some fashion—fortunately the offender in question offers a Markdown option—to provide for the agent. This needs to be done for every endpoint!

Just remove the authentication requirement for docs. You’re wasting your own time and resources just so everyone else can waste their own time and resources. This is a lose-lose scenario.

Show of hands. Who likes handwriting API clients? If your hand is up, I don’t believe you. The OpenAPI specification has existed for 15 years. Publishing an API without one is just disrespectful at this point. Why don’t you like me? Why do you want to make my life harder when I’m trying to give you money? Help me help you. Give me a spec so I can generate a typed client and focus on my business.

Oh, “here’s a Postman collection,” you say? I guess something is better than nothing, but now I have to figure out how to convert that to an OpenAPI spec. Why are we wasting time with an inferior format? Give me the good stuff!

This is similar to gated docs. APIs need credentials. Duh. Let me generate/rotate them on my own. Why do I need to wait multiple weeks for the IT team to generate credentials, flip a flag, or whatever? Stuff happens. Sometimes we need to rotate credentials. Don’t make me file a support ticket for a potential security incident! That means an issue that crops up on Saturday probably isn’t getting fixed until mid-day Monday when someone reads the ticket.

So you created self-serve credential issuance. Cool. But wait! Now you tell me the credential is associated with the identity of the person that created the credential. Meaning…all logs are associated with that person, so it’s impossible to discern between API calls from our backend applications and calls made by that person in your web app? Meaning…that person is the only one that can rotate the credentials, and we can’t simply follow the bad practice of sharing credentials because your application requires SSO and we have to draw the line somewhere at account sharing? Meaning…deactivating that person’s account will almost assuredly result in an incident?

I’m actively migrating away from an e-sign provider that does this because I am the person who set up the account, and am currently on vacation, and blocking folks from seeing contracts, because of course I want all the contracts sent to grocers to be associated with my account! My list of questions and criteria for vendors increases.

Webhooks are great for building realtime-ish workflows. Love ‘em. I have no love for the aforementioned e-sign provider that wants to verify webhook endpoints before saving them. “What is this verification”, you ask? It’s simple (and stupid): the provider sends a payload to the endpoint and only saves the new webhook configuration if the endpoint returns a successful response.

One of the first sections in any webhook integration guide covers security. Always validate the payload with a shared secret, and reject invalid payloads without processing. Well…it’s hard to validate without that shared secret, and the provider won’t give me a shared secret until the endpoint is verified to work. 🙃

This was the ridiculous workaround for a problem that doesn’t need to exist:

I wrote a support ticket for this, and the folks who responded didn’t quite understand why this was a problematic workflow. They do understand that I am migrating away from their product, however, and suddenly want to chat to get feedback.

It’s worth noting that I haven’t even discussed the API schemas and resources. Most companies get this right for their RESTful APIs with understandable nouns and verbs that define the business concepts and actions. Older payments companies continue to struggle with this for some inexplicable reason despite having over 15 years to just copy Stripe. Seriously, just copy the Stripe API. We spent a lot of time and energy building it. It’s good. Take it.

I’m just happy folks are building APIs, even with the horrible developer experience. We’ve largely eliminated a 40+ step process in about four weeks. Sure, agents wrote the code in like 4 hours and most of that four weeks was waiting for credentials, but progress is progress.

它们各自都有各种各样的问题。如果这些 API 面向的是新领域、承担的是新颖工作，那多少还可以接受；但这些解决方案都已经存在了十年甚至更久。更令人沮丧的是，开发者完全可以直接借鉴现有的、更优秀的 API 和实践，从而做得更好！

下面是一些我个人特别反感的问题。

如果我必须登录才能阅读你的 API 文档，那你已经搞砸了。你们居然真的写了文档，这一点值得肯定，但我为什么还要登录！？为了阅读文档，我不得不中断当前工作流，填写表单或给你们的支持团队发邮件，然后等待几个小时甚至几天！？

我曾向一个团队抱怨过这件事，他们也承认给文档设置访问门槛并不理想。不过，一位高管想要追踪潜在客户。搞什么！？我们已经是客户了。这个潜在客户已经赢单了。还有什么可追踪的！？

在代理式开发中，这个问题更加严重。我更愿意直接提供文档链接，让代理自行探索模式、构建客户端并完成集成。但设置访问门槛会打断这一流程。现在我不得不以某种方式下载文档——幸运的是，相关服务提供商提供 Markdown 格式——再把文档交给代理。每个端点都要这样处理！

直接取消文档的身份验证要求吧。你们这是在浪费自己的时间和资源，只为了让其他人也浪费他们的时间和资源。这是一个双输局面。

举手示意一下：有谁喜欢手写 API 客户端？如果你举手了，我不信。OpenAPI 规范已经存在 15 年了。到了现在，发布一个没有 OpenAPI 规范的 API，简直就是对人的不尊重。你为什么不喜欢我？我想给你钱的时候，你为什么要让我的日子更难过？帮帮我，也就是帮你自己。给我一份规范，这样我就能生成类型化客户端，把精力集中在自己的业务上。

哦，你说“这里有一份 Postman 集合”？我想，有总比没有好，但现在我还得想办法把它转换成 OpenAPI 规范。我们为什么要在一种低劣的格式上浪费时间？把好东西给我！

这和给文档设置访问门槛是类似的问题。API 需要凭证。废话，当然需要。让我自己生成和轮换凭证吧。为什么我得等上好几周，等 IT 团队生成凭证、切换某个开关，或者做类似的事情？事情总会发生。有时我们需要轮换凭证。不要让我为了一个潜在的安全事件提交支持工单！这意味着，周六出现的问题，很可能要等到周一中午有人看到工单后才能解决。

所以，你们创建了自助式凭证签发功能。很好。但等等！现在你又告诉我，这个凭证与创建它的人的身份绑定。也就是说……所有日志都归属于这个人，因此根本无法区分来自我们后端应用的 API 调用和这个人在你们 Web 应用中发起的调用？也就是说……只有这个人能够轮换凭证，而由于你们的应用要求单点登录（SSO），并且我们总得在账户共享这类糟糕做法上划条线，所以我们不能简单地共享凭证？也就是说……停用这个人的账户几乎肯定会导致一次事故？

我正在积极迁离一家采用这种做法的电子签名服务商，因为我是那个设置账户的人，而我目前正在休假；结果大家都无法查看合同——当然了，我当然希望所有发给杂货商的合同都关联到我的账户！我对供应商的疑问和筛选标准又增加了。

Webhook 非常适合构建近实时的工作流。我喜欢它们。但对于前面提到的那家电子签名服务商，我可是一点好感都没有：它要求在保存 Webhook 之前先验证端点。“你问什么叫验证？”很简单（也很愚蠢）：服务商向该端点发送一个负载，只有当端点返回成功响应时，服务商才会保存新的 Webhook 配置。

任何 Webhook 集成指南最前面的章节之一都会讲安全性。始终使用共享密钥验证负载，并在不进行处理的情况下拒绝无效负载。可是……没有共享密钥就很难完成验证，而服务商在端点被验证为可正常工作之前，又不会给我共享密钥。🙃

这就是为一个本不需要存在的问题设计出的荒谬变通方案：

我为此提交了一张支持工单，但回复我的人似乎不太明白这种工作流程为什么有问题。不过，他们确实明白我正在迁离他们的产品，于是突然想找我聊天，听取反馈。

值得一提的是，我甚至还没讨论 API 的模式和资源。大多数公司在 RESTful API 这方面做得都不错：用易于理解的名词和动词来定义业务概念与操作。尽管已经有超过 15 年的时间可以直接照搬 Stripe，老牌支付公司却出于某种令人费解的原因，仍然在这方面苦苦挣扎。真的，直接照搬 Stripe API 吧。我们花了大量时间和精力把它做出来。它很好用。拿去吧。

即使开发者体验糟糕透顶，我还是很高兴有人在构建 API。我们大体上在四周左右消除了一个包含 40 多个步骤的流程。当然，代理大约只用了 4 个小时就写完了代码，而这四周里的大部分时间都在等待凭证；但进步就是进步。

evidence.quote: I have had the displeasure of integrating with a few different APIs over the past few weeks while working to automate Vori’s onboarding flow. These APIs have been for systems including contract rendering and e-signature collection, invoicing/billing systems, CRMs, card processors and gateways, and card terminal providers.
The OpenAPI specification has existed for 15 years.
I’m actively migrating away from an e-sign provider that does this because I am the person who set up the account, and am currently on vacation, and blocking folks from seeing contracts

One of the first sections in any webhook integration guide covers security. Always validate the payload with a shared secret, and reject invalid payloads without processing. Well…it’s hard to validate without that shared secret, and the provider won’t give me a shared secret until the endpoint is verified to work.
We’ve largely eliminated a 40+ step process in about four weeks. Sure, agents wrote the code in like 4 hours and most of that four weeks was waiting for credentials, but progress is progress.
